INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: A volatile-anesthetic-associated rise in carbon dioxide with muscle rigidity can indicate an MH crisis.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Suspected MH calls for prompt trigger withdrawal and dantrolene alongside oxygenation and coordinated emergency support.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: MH-related muscle injury can release potassium and cause cardiotoxic ECG changes.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: One independently checked publication directly connects MH-associated potassium release to the ECG pattern.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Intravenous calcium salts provide acute cardiac protection in severe hyperkalemia.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Calcium does not remove potassium; potassium-lowering treatment must accompany cardiac protection.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Single government source for this mechanism; the MH guidelines independently support combined potassium treatment.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: The dantrolene precaution concerns calcium-channel-blocking drugs; the same MH guidance includes calcium gluconate for hyperkalemia.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Single direct guideline for this drug-class distinction; independently cross-checked calcium use in EMHG, without importing MHAUS content.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Persistent or recurring hypermetabolic MH signs can require additional dantrolene.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Amiodarone can be used for ventricular tachyarrhythmias in the appropriate resuscitation context.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Institutional cognitive-aid support; not a claim that every broad QRS needs amiodarone.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Unexpected perioperative hypotension with bronchospasm should prompt consideration of anaphylaxis.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Perioperative antibiotics are potential anaphylaxis triggers; the bedside syndrome does not prove a specific culprit.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: In monitored perioperative anaphylaxis, trained anesthesia clinicians use titrated intravenous epinephrine with intravenous crystalloid resuscitation.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: No dose or dilution is scored; this is not a community or unmonitored IV administration recommendation.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Inhaled bronchodilators can supplement treatment of anaphylactic bronchospasm but do not substitute for epinephrine in associated shock.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Persistent cardiovascular compromise after epinephrine boluses supports an epinephrine infusion with ongoing volume resuscitation and monitoring.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Bolus thresholds and infusion regimens vary; none is invented or scored.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: A second vasopressor may be added when anaphylactic shock remains refractory to epinephrine infusion and fluid resuscitation.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Both publications support escalation; exact agent preference is not ranked.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Corticosteroid administration is not a replacement for immediate epinephrine resuscitation of perioperative anaphylactic shock.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: The sources differ on routine later corticosteroid use; that disputed teaching point is withheld.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Smoke or visible glowing material in an airway tube during airway electrosurgery can signal an airway fire.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: An airway fire requires rapid interruption of airway gas flow and removal of the tracheal tube.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Water or saline is used to extinguish an airway fire before ventilation is re-established.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Stanford directly supports intraluminal saline; Pennsylvania independently supports extinguishing fire and safe airway restoration, but its tube-extinguishing wording is narrower.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: After an airway fire, bronchoscopic airway inspection assesses injury and allows residual debris removal.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Stanford explicitly recommends whole-airway bronchoscopy; Pennsylvania supports airway damage/debris assessment. No test sensitivity or mandatory flexible-versus-rigid choice is asserted.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in monitored perioperative care; hospital record facts remain historical, not local clinic capability.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: Bicarbonate may be used for relevant metabolic complications during a malignant hyperthermia crisis.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: The sources include bicarbonate among complication treatments; no exact acid-base threshold, dosing regimen or equivalence to calcium cardiac protection is asserted.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult perioperative care; the airway-fire scene is an outside hospital record.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: When surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis is indicated, administration before skin incision is consistent with guideline practice.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: One independently checked society guideline for this chronology; no exact timing interval, agent regimen or repeat-dose rule is authored.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult perioperative care; the airway-fire scene is an outside hospital record.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: A planned controlled extubation in an at-risk adult can use an airway exchange catheter to preserve temporary reintubation access.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Single contemporary society guideline for the controlled technique; not a recommendation to prepare such a catheter during an active airway fire.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult perioperative care; the airway-fire scene is an outside hospital record.

INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.statement: The immediate airway-fire response removes the involved tube; a planned extubation access-preservation sequence is not a prerequisite to that removal.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.limitation: Comparative clinical application of separate emergency-removal and controlled-extubation guidance, not a directly studied head-to-head sequence. Exact distractor ranking needs clinician review.
INTRAOP_I11_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult perioperative care; the airway-fire scene is an outside hospital record.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: A stable adult with a localized perianal abscess may undergo ambulatory drainage.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: Individual suitability, staffing and anesthesia assessment are still required; no size or vital-sign cutoff is proposed.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: During acute abscess drainage, a suspected fistula that cannot be demonstrated is not an indication for deliberate probing through unestablished tissue planes.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: One adequate guideline directly supports this exact exploration boundary; independent procedural corroboration was not obtained.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: Inflammatory distortion around an acute abscess can make exploratory probing create an unintended passage.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: This describes a potential harm, not a measured risk or an inevitable outcome.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: An established simple low fistula with preserved continence can be suitable for lay-open treatment in selected patients.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: The reused ASCRS source was accessed 2026-11-11; mapping was checked locally 2026-11-12. In Crohn disease the rectal inflammatory state adds a separate eligibility condition.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: In Crohn fistula care, current rectal inflammation changes the suitability and timing of tract closure even when the tract is low and continence is preserved.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly verified disease-specific guideline; comparative studies are limited. The draft uses marked current ulceration rather than asserting a universal endoscopic threshold.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: A rectal advancement flap is a selected closure option in Crohn fistula care when proctitis is absent.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly verified disease-specific guideline; the statement does not establish the best flap technique or a healing probability.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: A loose draining seton can preserve fistula drainage while medical and surgical care for Crohn disease is coordinated.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: Staging is not a claim that an indefinite seton by itself cures Crohn fistulizing disease. No drug choice or seton-removal interval is authored.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: Changed anal symptoms in chronic perianal Crohn disease warrant renewed evaluation for a possible fistula-associated malignancy.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: The relevant recommendation relies on expert opinion and rare-disease data; symptoms are not diagnostic of cancer. No surveillance interval or risk percentage is proposed.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: A suspicious lesion found during reassessment of chronic perianal Crohn disease should be sampled, including tract sampling under anesthesia when required.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: The independent source is an illustrative case report, not comparative evidence for a particular biopsy depth, number or technique.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: A benign result from one sampled anorectal site does not determine the histology of a separate abnormal tract focus.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: This is a specimen-provenance inference supported by the distinct specimen diagnoses in one case report and the guideline requirement to sample suspicious lesions. It is not a claimed false-negative rate.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing anorectal EUA; Crohn-specific claims apply only to the explicitly described Crohn case.
verificationLocators: Kaneshiro separate rectal and tract specimens

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: When an obvious fistula encountered at abscess drainage involves sphincter muscle, a loose draining seton is an option for staged care.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: WSES recommendation is weak and based on low-quality evidence. This does not justify searching for an unconfirmed passage.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with an obvious muscle-involving fistula at anorectal abscess drainage.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.statement: The incision used for anorectal abscess drainage must continue to provide drainage as the wound heals.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: One guideline supplies the targeted open-drainage principle; no packing, catheter, closure interval or healing timetable is selected.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults after operative drainage of a localized anorectal abscess.

INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.limitation: Exact patient-specific comparison remains needs_clinician_review. One guideline may supply the deciding comparative atom; source plurality is not represented as trial-level corroboration.
INTRAOP_ANORECTAL_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the represented diagnostic or treatment phase.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Before dilation over a guidewire, establish that the wire is in the intended venous path.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Current consensus and an older concordant cross-check; not comparative evidence of one confirmation test over every possible alternative.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Evidence obtained from an earlier needle position does not by itself establish the location of a subsequently threaded wire.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Temporal/device inference from staged confirmation guidance; no claim that the supplied ambiguous echo proves arterial entry.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Ultrasound can follow a wire within the accessible target vein before tract dilation; complementary views help establish its relationship to vessel walls.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Accessible-neck confirmation is not proof of an entire intrathoracic trajectory; persistent uncertainty still requires resolution before dilation.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Pressure waveform or blood-gas evidence can contribute to identifying the compartment sampled by an access needle; blood color alone is insufficient.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: ASA2012 is a superseded technical cross-check for the blood-gas method; the question tests the limited time/device represented, not a gas cutoff.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: An inadvertently placed large-bore arterial dilator or sheath should remain in position pending urgent vascular or interventional removal planning.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Consensus supported by complication reports, not randomized evidence; device and vessel-specific controlled removal require specialist judgment.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: The 2025 Association guidance specifically retains inadvertently arterial devices of at least 6 Fr; an 8-Fr sheath is on that side of the boundary.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single current source for this exact size boundary. Eight Fr is the constructed device characteristic, not an invented practice cutoff. Small-needle compression is not generalized to a dilated tract.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Immediate extraction of a large arterial device can produce serious vascular complications before a controlled removal strategy is established.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Case-based complication evidence; no numerical risk or inevitable harm is asserted.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Changing to a smaller device does not substitute for an individualized specialist plan to control an enlarged arterial tract.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Application of the retention/removal rule; no source establishes a universal prohibition on wire use within a specialist repair strategy.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A catheter in an internal thoracic venous route may project near the SVC frontally while an orthogonal view shows an anterior parasternal course.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly verified publication for this precise imaging boundary. Constructed text findings are original; no image or figure is reproduced.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Intravascular position in a small tributary does not establish the intended long-term central port position.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: No exact SVC/cavoatrial distance or high-right-atrial recommendation is taught; acceptable tip targets vary among sources.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A recognized malpositioned port catheter needs correction or replacement rather than acceptance solely because blood can be aspirated.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Technical guidance supports correction; the exact maneuver depends on actual anatomy, device and operator capability. No blind withdrawal is proposed.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Blood aspiration establishes access to blood but cannot distinguish a central course from an intravascular tributary course.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Anatomical application of imaging/flow confirmation guidance. This does not negate limited emergency use exceptions for temporary catheters.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Demonstrated central patency favors attempting image-guided correction through usable access before obtaining a new puncture solely for branch malposition.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Clinical application, not a head-to-head trial proving one salvage technique. A failed correction, device damage, occlusion or injury changes the route decision.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing planned central venous access/port placement; no pediatric dosing, neonatal or hospital reconstruction objective.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Documented anatomical markers attached to a skin excision permit localization of the corresponding margins for pathology.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Marker meaning must be documented and preserved; the claims do not prescribe a single universal suture code.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing an already planned superficial skin/soft-tissue excision; no sarcoma resection or infant extrapolation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Fragmentation and loss of reconstructable orientation limit anatomical margin assignment without automatically invalidating separately preserved specimen information.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The exact detached-fat scenario is a constructed provenance inference; needs surgeon/pathologist confirmation. Fragmentation does not mean the tissue is diagnostically useless.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing an already planned superficial skin/soft-tissue excision; no sarcoma resection or infant extrapolation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Knowing where a detached specimen originated is different from knowing which of its indistinguishable faces was the final boundary.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: General specimen-orientation principle; the source does not verify the fictional patient geometry. No histological positive/negative result is inferred.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing an already planned superficial skin/soft-tissue excision; no sarcoma resection or infant extrapolation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: For a separately removed bed sample, the new final margin is the surface cut from tissue that remains in the patient, distinct from the old cavity-facing surface.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly verified guideline for the cavity/new-face distinction; guideline is breast-specific. Geometrical application to an already planned skin bed sample is an explicit extrapolation, not a resection-extent recommendation.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing an already planned superficial skin/soft-tissue excision; no sarcoma resection or infant extrapolation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A specimen suture may identify the cavity-facing surface or the new margin; its actual documented designation governs interpretation.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Both conventions are directly allowed by RCPath. Skin sources corroborate documented orientation, not the exact separate-bed workflow.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing an already planned superficial skin/soft-tissue excision; no sarcoma resection or infant extrapolation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A recognized needle-only arterial puncture can be managed by needle withdrawal and digital compression, with further assessment if complications develop.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly verified older society source for the counterfactual; this is not permission to remove an arterial sheath or any neck/chest arterial catheter without specialist planning.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with an immediately recognized, compressible needle-only puncture before tract dilation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A systemic arterial waveform from an access device supports arterial positioning even when the return looks dark.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Technical interpretation; transducer setup and simultaneous imaging matter. No unverified pressure cutoff or claim based on color alone.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at a central-access confirmation checkpoint.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Doppler characterization of blood flow around a local wire echo does not by itself demonstrate the wire staying within the target vein along an obscured segment.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked independent review separates flow/vessel characterization from wire-position confirmation. The ranking is a technical application to the stated local observation, not a claim that Doppler is never useful during wire assessment. Current wire-course guidance is separately supported by the retained AoA2025 claim.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing jugular guidewire assessment before tract dilation.

ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Compressibility helps assess a venous segment and its patency; testing a neighboring segment does not establish the retained guidewire trajectory through a different obscured region.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked independent technical review supports the function distinction. No compression threshold, force, pressure or universal exclusion criterion is added; the current task concerns the instrument course, not a thrombosis rule.
ASC_ACCESS_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing jugular guidewire assessment before tract dilation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Unexplained bile encountered during cholecystectomy should prompt assessment for a bile-duct injury.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Single guideline explicitly supports this operative trigger; the synthetic stream location is not a diagnostic classification.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: When duct injury is suspected during cholecystectomy, intraoperative duct imaging can clarify the anatomy before further operative decisions.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: IOC is the offered method, not a claim that it universally outperforms intraoperative ultrasound or that equipment is installed.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: A separated main duct with tissue loss is a different repair problem from a small lateral defect with preserved duct continuity.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: No injury grade, exact gap-size threshold or universal reconstruction is inferred from the constructed observations.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: For an intraoperatively recognized bile-duct injury beyond local HPB expertise, control of bile contamination and transfer for specialist management are appropriate.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Current specialist guidance supports temporization; it does not make delayed repair mandatory for every injury or forbid expert index-operation repair.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Primary local repair can be appropriate for selected minor injuries; major tissue-loss injuries require a different plan and appropriate reconstructive expertise.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Exact reconstruction, timing and advanced endoscopic/radiologic options belong to the specialist team. A conventional papillary stent must not be assumed to bridge an unconnected proximal system.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: When a gallbladder lesion is suspicious, retrieval should limit specimen disruption and bile contamination, using a bag rather than relying on an unprotected extraction.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: One consensus publication is used. Enlarging the extraction incision instead of puncturing or crushing this particular specimen is an authored application requiring surgeon sign-off, not a directly tested comparative rule.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Final gallbladder-cancer decisions depend on pathological invasion depth and margins, rather than the operative appearance of a wall lesion by itself.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Coverage boundary only; no live ASC cancer-staging or radical-resection simulation is proposed.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Expert-confirmed completely removed margin-negative T1a gallbladder cancer does not automatically require completion radical resection.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Cross-check of preserved bank coverage, not a new question or an assertion about inadequate histology or deeper invasion.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: For suitable patients with incidental gallbladder cancer extending into perimuscular tissue, completion oncologic surgery may include liver-bed resection and regional lymphadenectomy.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Preserved T2 coverage only. Exact extent, timing and duct resection depend on staging and margin findings; no numeric rule added.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy or subsequent specialist pathology review; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: During cholecystectomy, reliable identification of the cystic structures should precede their clipping or division.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: This supports the baseline operative plan, not a claim that prior identification rules out a subsequently suspected injury. No new CVS-only question is authored.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: An otherwise controlled laparoscopic injury assessment does not itself require open conversion for fuller diagnostic staging.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: One guideline directly addresses this boundary. Conversion remains appropriate when exposure or control cannot be maintained laparoscopically; no universal prohibition is taught.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or recognized duct injury during cholecystectomy.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: A routine transpapillary stent does not by itself establish drainage from a proximal duct system that lacks a continuous luminal connection to the distal duct.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: This distinguishes ordinary communicating-leak diversion from a disconnected system. It does not exclude specialist rendezvous, endoscopic/radiological combinations or other selected nonoperative injury management.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with main-duct discontinuity documented during or after cholecystectomy.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Contrast duct imaging requires an injection route that communicates with the target ducts; an opening below a closed gallbladder-side clip provides a different route from injection into the isolated gallbladder.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Sources describe cystic-duct and gallbladder injection. The closed-clip comparison is a direct anatomical application to constructed observations, not a tested superiority estimate; actual site safety requires clinician review.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy with the represented operative anatomy and local resources; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: When assessing a suspected operative duct leak through usable duct access, contrast cholangiography can delineate luminal continuity and contrast escape, while ICG fluorescence principally supplies anatomical orientation.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: IOC over fluorescence is a conditional low-certainty preference; fluorescence is not prohibited, and this does not rank IOC over expert laparoscopic ultrasound. Clinical confirmation of the specific option ranking is needed.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy with the represented operative anatomy and local resources; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: Confirmed CBD stones found during cholecystectomy may be cleared operatively or by postoperative ERCP, with anatomy, available expertise and resources informing the route.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: One adequate society review is used for the exact route-selection teaching point; an independently licensed second management source was not established. The review does not mandate a single technique for every patient.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy with the represented operative anatomy and local resources; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: A small or friable cystic duct weighs against transcystic stone extraction even when a guidewire can enter the common duct.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Single-review support; direct observation of splitting tissue is constructed and requires surgeon confirmation. Wire-versus-basket traversal is an anatomical application rather than an exact quantified failure rule.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy with the represented operative anatomy and local resources; no pediatric extrapolation.

INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.statement: The cited SAGES review favors a common duct at least 7 mm wide for transductal exploration to reduce postoperative stricture risk.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.limitation: Single-review selection criterion, not a biological cliff or universal ban on narrower-duct surgery. The synthetic 5-mm value is an observed case measurement, not a new guideline threshold.
INTRAOP_BILIARY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cholecystectomy with the represented operative anatomy and local resources; no pediatric extrapolation.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Seeing tissue outside the gut through an endoscopic wall gap supports recognition of a full-thickness injury.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Constructed observations are not diagnostic photographs or a validated image classifier.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: A promptly recognized small colonic defect with good preparation and feasible tissue capture can be treated with endoscopic clips by an experienced operator.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Device feasibility and contamination matter. Single adequate guideline publication; no universal clip-versus-surgery superiority is asserted.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Stable patients with a sealed colonic injury, localized symptoms and no diffuse free fluid may receive monitored hospital nonoperative care.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Selected inpatient care, not outpatient discharge; initial stability does not ensure success.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Poor preparation, gross contamination or a large defect that cannot be reliably closed favors urgent surgical management of colonoscopy perforation.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Single guideline publication supports this composite boundary; no size-only mandatory-operation threshold is taught.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Free peritoneal gas by itself does not require surgery after a colonic injury when other findings support nonoperative care.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: No demonstrated contrast leak does not prove durable sealing; serial reassessment remains necessary.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Hospital nonoperative care after colonic perforation includes bowel rest, intravenous hydration, broad-spectrum antibiotics and close reassessment.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: No drug, dose, duration, discharge time or feeding interval is supplied.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Worsening physiology, peritoneal signs or an ongoing colonic leak after attempted closure requires prompt surgical reassessment.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Apparent endoscopic success must not delay escalation. The eventual operation is not prescribed.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: An esophageal perforation recognized during endoscopy should receive feasible endoscopic closure; clips can close a small defect.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Single adequate permitted guideline publication. Constructed edges approximate; no ranking of through-the-scope versus over-the-scope clips is offered.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Covered esophageal stents can address larger defects or an unsatisfactory clip closure.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Patient-specific alternative, not a prohibition on stenting all small injuries. Exact clip-versus-stent ranking needs review.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Esophageal injuries that cannot be safely managed nonoperatively require operative source control.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Hospital care; no hospital operation is enacted in the ASC.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Pressurized intraperitoneal gas can impair ventilation and venous return, producing abdominal distension with respiratory and circulatory compromise.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Case-report physiology and society cross-check; not a diagnostic-accuracy estimate.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Emergency percutaneous release of intraperitoneal gas can temporize cardiovascular and respiratory compromise from tension pneumoperitoneum.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Expert rescue, not a standardized device, entry-site or needle-size rule. Primary case evidence is limited.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Improvement after gas decompression does not establish durable closure of the underlying gastrointestinal injury.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: The primary report required surgery; that outcome is not generalized to every successfully clipped injury. Hospital source-control assessment remains necessary.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with iatrogenic gastrointestinal wall injury; pressure physiology is applied to the constructed adult procedural case.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: A gastric tube decompresses the stomach lumen rather than the peritoneal space.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.limitation: Anatomical inference supported by the reported persistence of a tense abdomen despite gastric-tube use; not a comparative trial.
ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastrointestinal perforation in the stated procedural context.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Esophageal perforation care includes withheld oral intake, antimicrobial/supportive treatment and access to expert surgical assessment.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastrointestinal perforation in the stated procedural context.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: In a stable patient with localized findings, contrast CT can assess colonic leakage and free fluid when considering nonoperative care.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastrointestinal perforation in the stated procedural context.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.statement: Prompt colonic closure and careful insufflation can reduce further gas escape outside the bowel.

ENDOSCOPIC_INJURY_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastrointestinal perforation in the stated procedural context.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Retching-associated Mallory-Weiss injury produces a longitudinal mucosal split around the gastroesophageal junction.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly read technical review supports this morphology. It supports the fictional lesion description, not image interpretation or proof that every junctional split has this cause.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: CAG 2025 suggests observation rather than routine endoscopic hemostasis for a Mallory-Weiss tear bearing a nonbleeding visible vessel.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: CAG recommendation 7A is conditional with very low certainty. Kim's older technical review corroborates the dry-vessel boundary with coagulopathy/rebleeding exceptions. Restrict application to the supplied stable, dry, noncoagulopathic story; no universal ban on treatment.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: For an actively bleeding Mallory-Weiss tear, CAG supports clipping or band ligation rather than epinephrine as the sole hemostatic treatment.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: CAG 5/6A/6B: conditional, very low certainty. Kim cross-checks mechanical treatment and injection limitations. Neither source establishes a unique clip-versus-band ranking; both remain counterfactual alternatives.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: A peptic ulcer with a nonbleeding visible vessel warrants endoscopic hemostasis, unlike routine treatment of a dry Mallory-Weiss tear.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: The ulcer part is directly supported by the 2026 guideline. The tear part retains CAG's very-low-certainty limitation. Distinct lesions explain the boundary; no new ulcer item or fixed regimen is authored.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: A projecting platelet-fibrin plug on an esophageal varix is evidence of recent variceal hemorrhage even when the viewed surface is temporarily dry.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Both primary society guidelines directly describe plug/nipple stigmata. A fictional written endoscopy record supplies the observation; it is not a validated image-reading examination.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Band ligation is the preferred initial endoscopic treatment for acute esophageal variceal hemorrhage when ligation can be performed.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Society recommendations favor ligation over injection sclerotherapy. Sclerotherapy remains an alternative when banding is not feasible; no absolute ineffectiveness claim is made.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Cardiofundal variceal hemorrhage has a different endoscopic treatment pathway from esophageal variceal hemorrhage.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly checked source for the feedback comparison: cyanoacrylate is an established gastric option. This does not rank direct glue against EUS-guided therapy or radiologic treatment in 2026. That prospective target is withheld pending a current rights-permitted comparison.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Persistent esophageal variceal bleeding despite vasoactive treatment and endoscopic hemostasis calls for urgent rescue TIPS assessment.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Rescue TIPS is supplied as the hospital team's plan, not simulated at the ASC or ranked against other definitive options. No severity score, futility threshold or preemptive timing rule is taught.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: A dedicated removable covered esophageal metal stent can temporarily tamponade refractory esophageal variceal bleeding while definitive therapy is arranged.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Bridge use is supported but comparative evidence is limited. A dedicated hemostasis device, trained team and protected airway are part of the outside record. Not any generic esophageal stent and not definitive portal decompression.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Balloon tamponade is another accepted temporary bridge for uncontrolled esophageal variceal bleeding.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: ESGE weakly favors a covered stent where available; BSG retains either bridge. Balloon is intentionally not a scored distractor. No inflation, traction, volume or dwell-time protocol is provided.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Covered esophageal hemostasis stents treat esophageal rather than gastric variceal bleeding and require surveillance for migration.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: This is a location and follow-up boundary, not a promise of durable control or a scored bedside-recovery encounter.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Acute variceal hemorrhage requires hospital support, with vasoactive and antibacterial treatment and airway protection when clinically indicated.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: Background context only. No doses, regimens, transfusion thresholds or inpatient medication algorithm is scored. The clinic only reviews the outside record.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described fictional endoscopy checkpoints; no pediatric extrapolation.

I16_CLAIMS.statement: Esophageal injection sclerotherapy delivers sclerosant into variceal tissue and can be used when ligation is unsuitable.
I16_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked multisociety EIS subsection supports the varix-level target and fallback role. It does not impose a pinpoint-vessel requirement, quantify adequate visibility or directly compare every rescue technique in this constructed blood-obscured scene. That application requires named clinical review.
I16_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults with esophageal varices; technical cross-check only, without a new regimen, dose or timing rule.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Repeated unintended pancreatic instrumentation during biliary ERCP increases concern for post-ERCP pancreatitis.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Qualitative procedural risk only; no exact probability, demographic weighting or attempt threshold authored.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Temporary pancreatic duct stenting is supported for high-risk ERCP, including repeated pancreatic access, even after rectal NSAID prophylaxis.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: The additive-to-NSAID boundary has one direct current society source. Yin independently supports stenting in selected high-risk adults but not that incremental comparison. Technical placement and follow-up need clinician review.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Increasing intravenous fluid prophylaxis does not replace the indicated pancreatic stent decision after high-risk pancreatic instrumentation.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Limited ranking from the current recommendation to add a stent; no universal head-to-head inferiority of hydration, fluid regimen or contraindication protocol claimed.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Several advanced approaches can be used for difficult biliary cannulation; the access history by itself does not establish one universal best technique.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Consensus names precut, double-wire and transpancreatic approaches. No unverified morphology rule, competence cutoff or rescue hierarchy is keyed.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Contrast escaping beside a fresh sphincterotomy can indicate a periampullary ERCP injury, distinct from a distant duodenal-wall tear.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Primary cohort context supports injury type. The fictional contrast observation is not a fluoroscopic image or proof of precise defect dimensions.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Suspected upper gastrointestinal procedural perforation requires hospital monitoring, fasting, intravenous supportive care and antibiotics with multidisciplinary assessment.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Shared background care only. No regimen, dose, duration, feeding study or discharge criteria prescribed.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: A stable patient with an immediately recognized periampullary injury and established biliary access can be managed initially with transpapillary bile diversion.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Injury- and physiology-dependent. DGVS gives a general selection framework; the primary cohort supplies ERCP experience. No universal advantage over surgery or percutaneous routes asserted.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Conventional diversion and covered metal stents are both used for type II ERCP injury; comparative cohort findings do not establish a universal covered-stent advantage.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: One small retrospective cohort; nonsignificance is not equivalence. Device superiority remains unkeyed, including in view of differing conclusions in a restricted-license cohort excluded from new evidence.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: A localized fluid collection can require separate source control despite functioning transpapillary biliary drainage.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: One primary cohort reports collection drainage. Duct drainage and extraluminal collection drainage are separate targets; no frequency or guaranteed outcome inferred.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: A symptomatic localized retroperitoneal collection after ERCP injury can be treated with image-guided catheter drainage when the patient's condition and access route permit.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: ERCP-specific evidence is observational. Current guidance treats failed or infeasible catheter drainage as an escalation boundary; no catheter dimensions or exact route prescribed.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: Worsening condition, generalized peritoneal findings or failed nonsurgical source control after endoscopic perforation supports prompt operative management.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Exact escalation boundary uses one current society consensus. No universal incision, repair, reconstruction or numeric physiological trigger specified.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: CT can characterize extraluminal fluid and continuing leakage after suspected endoscopic perforation to inform treatment selection.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: Already acquired outside hospital observations only. No enacted test, oral-contrast dose, sensitivity estimate or delay introduced.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

I18_CLAIMS.statement: An injury observed at an incised papillary margin is a periampullary injury context, distinct from injury to the upstream duct wall by instrumentation.
I18_CLAIMS.limitation: The primary cohort distinguishes perivaterian injury from ductal and distant wall injury. The exact new cut-margin observations are constructed record data requiring clinical confirmation; no real fluoroscopic image, defect measurement or device-superiority inference is supplied.
I18_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adult hospital ERCP; no pediatric extrapolation.

GROIN_INTRAOP_PARKED_CASE_DEFINITIONS.name: Victor Morgan
GROIN_INTRAOP_PARKED_CASE_DEFINITIONS.presentation: Victor Morgan, a 67-year-old man, is in clinic for review of the outside hospital operative record from his emergency groin hernia repair. The question concerns the recorded injury checkpoint before its treatment, rather than care in the clinic's OR.

nodes.objective: Use a recorded injury's compartment and viable tissue to choose repair rather than drainage or bladder resection.
nodes.currentUpdate: The outside emergency operation note records a gaping full-thickness opening at the bladder dome during dissection of a trapped groin hernia. Saline instilled through the catheter emerges directly into the peritoneal cavity. The edges bleed when touched and the tissue is supple; the opening is away from the trigone. This checkpoint precedes treatment of the injury.
nodes.stem: Which bladder plan fits the recorded injury at that checkpoint in Victor's outside emergency groin operation?

choices.label: Close the bladder defect and maintain urethral drainage
choices.rationale: The accessible intraperitoneal surgical defect calls for direct repair with bladder decompression. The observed edges support preserving and closing the bladder rather than removing a segment.
choices.temptation: Integrate the route of leakage and tissue findings, not just the fact that a catheter is already present.
choices.counterfactual: A small uncomplicated extraperitoneal leak could favor catheter-based management under specialist assessment.

choices.label: Drain around the bladder and maintain urethral drainage
choices.rationale: Drainage does not close this gaping intraperitoneal defect seen during the operation. Selected conservative pathways are not a general substitute for repairing a recognized major surgical opening.
choices.temptation: Overextend catheter management of selected contained or small injuries to a currently accessible major defect.
choices.counterfactual: Selected small uncomplicated injuries discovered after an operation may qualify for conservative care after specialist assessment.

choices.label: Resect the injured bladder segment and maintain urethral drainage
choices.rationale: The record describes supple perfused tissue. Herniation and a laceration do not establish a need to remove viable bladder wall rather than repair it.
choices.temptation: Treat any injured herniated organ as a segment requiring resection.
choices.counterfactual: Devitalized wall or a separate lesion requiring excision would change the tissue-preservation decision.

nodes.explanation: The operative record shows a full-thickness intraperitoneal bladder opening with viable edges. Direct repair with catheter decompression fits that checkpoint; a peritoneal drain does not replace closure, and this record supplies no devitalized segment requiring resection. The question does not select suture layers, catheter duration, mesh use or follow-up imaging.

gate.inference: Identify the intraperitoneal route from the saline finding, then use viable tissue to select direct repair rather than decompression or segment removal.
gate.cueAttack: Three plans share urethral drainage and comparable length. The diagnosis is not placed in the complaint. Raw leakage and tissue observations resolve two genuine boundaries without an author-written eligibility label.
gate.stageCategory: One immediate bladder treatment plan in a historical operative checkpoint; all options are named surgical or drainage plans.
gate.difficulty: Predicted moderate: a catheter already in place tempts conservative care; herniated tissue and a visible opening tempt unnecessary resection.
gate.decidingObservation: Saline exits into the peritoneal cavity through a gaping surgical defect whose edges remain supple and perfused.
gate.counterfactual: Change to a small contained uncomplicated extraperitoneal injury: catheter-based management becomes reasonable. Change to devitalized tissue: direct closure without addressing that tissue loses support.
gate.deletionTest: Without the leakage compartment, repair versus drainage is not resolved; without tissue viability, closure versus resection is less secure.
gate.sequenceCheck: Standalone clinic chart review. Every observation was already recorded outside the clinic; later treatment or outcome is not presented as knowledge at the checkpoint.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: The initial Veress pressure and free gas influx help assess intraperitoneal placement; an immediate high-pressure, minimal-inflow episode does not establish a working intraperitoneal cavity.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly verified multidisciplinary guideline; supporting initial-pressure study is observational. No invented numeric cutoff or case-specific flow threshold.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: When initial access has not been established, reassess the access route before continuing insufflation or advancing a trocar.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Original synthesis of placement confirmation and alternative-entry recommendations. Does not mandate one open or closed technique or a number of attempts.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Insufflation pressure decisions depend on entry phase, exposure and patient tolerance; pressure or flow adjustment is not a substitute for verified access or control of a developing complication.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: No universal safe-pressure number, automatic conversion trigger or exact flow prescription is asserted. Flow-control counterfactuals synthesize the reviewed pressure/flow relationship; no manufacturer-specific algorithm is asserted.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: A misplaced or loose port can permit extraperitoneal CO2 spread, with palpable tissue gas and additional systemic CO2 uptake.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Narrative evidence; these findings do not determine the exact anatomic route or exclude a concurrent thoracic complication.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Progressive tissue gas with a continuing CO2 rise warrants reducing the insufflation burden and evaluating the entry route while ventilation and cardiopulmonary assessment continue.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Pause-and-port-reassessment wording is an original practical synthesis. No directly verified trial ranks pause versus conversion in this exact fictional presentation; clinician review of the boundary is required.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: A gradual CO2 rise during insufflation can reflect absorbed gas; ventilatory adjustment with reassessment is appropriate for a stable isolated load, while new deterioration requires reconsidering the cause.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: General physiology and narrative management evidence, not proof that any particular patient has an uncomplicated course. No tidal-volume or respiratory-rate prescription.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Gas entering injured vessels at access can cause abrupt circulatory collapse, hypoxemia and changing expired CO2.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: The pattern warrants suspicion rather than a definitive diagnosis; ordinary pressure effects, hemorrhage and anesthetic causes remain part of emergency assessment.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Suspected CO2 embolism requires immediate cessation of insufflation and release of pneumoperitoneum alongside oxygenation and circulatory support.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: No current dedicated formal guideline was retrieved. Main direct source is a 2012 narrative review with independent case-report corroboration; source-control must not await confirmatory monitoring.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Expired CO2 may rise or fall during CO2 embolism, so its direction alone cannot establish or exclude the event.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: The corroborating publication is one case; no diagnostic accuracy estimate or obligatory biphasic sequence is implied.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Port placement can injure abdominal-wall vessels, and a visible tract-related stream supports a local source distinct from a deep expanding hematoma.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: The cannula release/re-seat response is constructed teaching data consistent with tamponade, not a validated diagnostic test.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: A visible abdominal-wall port bleed can be controlled locally under vision, including hemostatic suturing; escalation depends on source visibility, control and patient physiology.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Single directly verified narrative source for the named local suture technique. No technique-superiority claim; exact source localization and distractor ranking need clinician confirmation.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Trocar withdrawal under direct observation helps reveal bleeding temporarily hidden by the cannula or working pressure.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Technical guidance and narrative evidence; a temporarily quiet field is not an independently validated hemostasis test.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: An enlarging retroperitoneal hematoma with recurrent circulatory instability after access raises concern for uncontrolled major vascular injury.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Does not identify the injured vessel. Fictional recurrent response and visibility observations support the decision boundary rather than a numeric shock threshold.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: Major access bleeding that is not promptly exposed and controlled laparoscopically requires urgent open control and vascular assistance rather than prolonged ineffective minimally invasive attempts.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Current society advice plus independent narrative review. Selected stable, exposed injuries may permit laparoscopic repair; the draft supplies expansion, incomplete exposure and recurrent instability.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: An implicated trocar should remain in position during initial evaluation and exposure of a suspected access injury until removal can occur with control.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Direct society instruction supports retention; the possible tamponade rationale is also consistent with guideline withdrawal cautions. Not a rule to retain an instrument indefinitely after control.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; pediatric extrapolation excluded.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: The reviewed multidisciplinary guideline uses an initial Veress pressure below 10 mmHg followed by free CO2 inflow to support intraperitoneal placement before continued insufflation.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: The exact below-10 criterion was freshly checked in the source recommendations. Based on observational evidence; not a universal pressure target for a later operative phase. No exact flow or waiting interval is invented.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; no pediatric extrapolation.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: At completion, a bleeding check should release cannula tamponade under direct vision and reduce pneumoperitoneum pressure while arterial pressure is adequate.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Technical guidance plus two narrative reviews support the released-tamponade assessment. The exact fictional completion decision still needs clinician confirmation; no pressure number, blood-pressure cutoff or device-superiority rule is asserted.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; no pediatric extrapolation.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: When an access cannula remains at a suspected deep vascular injury, preserve its position during initial exposure until removal can occur with bleeding controlled.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Retention depends on the cannula actually remaining at the injury, not on the site of a previous track. The fictional outer-cannula/removed-obturator scene is constructed data and needs exact clinician confirmation.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; no pediatric extrapolation.

LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.statement: A port tract remaining dry after cannula withdrawal and reduced insufflation at adequate arterial pressure supports hemostatic completion; recurrent bleeding requires further local control before closure.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.limitation: Original application of guideline withdrawal checks and narrative completion guidance to constructed patient observations. These sources do not compare an extra suture with skin closure in this exact case; the conclusion is not a device-superiority rule and requires clinician confirmation.
LAP_ACCESS_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing abdominal laparoscopy; no pediatric extrapolation.

LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.learningObjective: Apply the initial opening-pressure criterion to choose placement reassessment instead of a delivery-control adjustment.

LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.displayName: Interrupt the insufflation source during abrupt collapse
LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.learningObjective: Apply immediate gas-source interruption and pressure release during abrupt insufflation-associated instability without requiring a definitive mechanism diagnosis.

LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.displayName: Use the completed port-tract check to choose the remaining treatment
LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.learningObjective: Interpret a post-treatment hemostasis check with tamponade released and decide whether additional local control is needed before closure.

LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.displayName: Preserve a suspected injury track while obtaining hospital vascular control
LAP_ACCESS_CONCEPTS.learningObjective: Use an expanding deep hematoma and recurrent instability to select controlled open exposure before withdrawing the access cannula that remains at the injury.
