I07_CLAIMS.statement: The developmental route shared by inferior parathyroid tissue and thymus makes the thyrothymic tract and thymus relevant sites for a missing inferior gland.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Location is variable; this does not prove a particular patient has an intrathymic adenoma.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: After an inferior gland is absent from the exposed lower-pole region, cervical thyrothymic exploration is a supported next search before more remote ectopic dissections.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Search-order recommendation rests on one technical review, with anatomical corroboration rather than an independent comparative guideline.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Paraesophageal and retroesophageal regions are recognized ectopic search sites for superior parathyroid tissue.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: No nerve-relation classification or absolute superior/inferior identity is taught.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Failure to find an expected gland is insufficient evidence for an intrathyroidal target; less destructive ectopic search and directed confirmation precede empirical thyroid resection.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Single adequate technical review. It describes reported empirical resection but cautions against blind procedures; no universal prohibition on thyroid surgery.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Conventional Miami interpretation compares the PTH result obtained 10 minutes after excision with the higher preincision or preexcision value and uses a decline greater than 50 percent.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Applies to the stated protocol and an adequately collected sample in sporadic PHPT; meeting it predicts an endpoint, not guaranteed durable cure.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Saline carried from an intravenous line into a PTH specimen can dilute the sample and produce a falsely low measured PTH.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: The size of the error is not inferable from a flush history; no correction factor or sample-discard volume is authored.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: When collection details raise a substantive dilution concern, a properly collected repeat PTH is needed before using the apparent fall to decide operative completion or further gland exploration.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Clinical synthesis of sample-integrity requirements, not a directly tested universal resampling algorithm; exact collection protocol and follow-up interval require the endocrine/anesthesia team.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Dividing thyroid-bound terminal vessels close to the thyroid capsule can retain parathyroid perfusion that proximal common-vessel ligation would interrupt.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Single adequate direct technical review for this exact branch comparison; applies to the observed branching anatomy, not an assertion of identical arterial supply in all patients.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: A parathyroid gland with a retained functioning blood supply is preferentially preserved in situ during thyroid surgery.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Macroscopic viability assessment is imperfect; preservation does not guarantee normal postoperative function.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Discoloration of a parathyroid gland does not by itself establish irreversible loss of viability.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: No color threshold or duration predicts permanent function; assess the pedicle and observed perfusion response.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Capsular decompression followed by fresh oozing and improvement in gland color supports persisting arterial inflow and relief of congestion.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Single direct technical review; these observations do not certify future function. No mandatory diagnostic incision is prescribed for every gland.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: A benign parathyroid gland inadvertently removed with a thyroid specimen is a candidate for intraoperative autotransplantation rather than disposal with the thyroid.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: JAES strong recommendation is based on low-certainty evidence. Histological identity, suitability and specimen sterility must be checked; graft success is not guaranteed.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Confirmed parathyroid tissue can be divided into small fragments and placed in a well-perfused muscle pocket, including sternocleidomastoid, for autotransplantation.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: No exact fragment size, number of pockets or universal preference over forearm grafting is authored.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: Histological confirmation of suspected parathyroid tissue can support selection of tissue for autotransplantation.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Single reviewed technical description. The case supplies a completed frozen-section report of benign parathyroid; no claim that morphology or PTH establishes absence of malignancy.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroid surgery, as specified by the claim; no pediatric inference.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: PTH measured in a nodule needle washout can identify parathyroid tissue; it does not establish that all hyperfunctioning tissue has been removed.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Tissue identity and the postoperative biochemical prediction from circulating PTH dynamics are different uses of the assay.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: A hypoechoic candidate with a polar feeding vessel and peripheral vascularity has a recognized parathyroid localization pattern.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: This pattern supports localization but does not prove histology or functional completeness; not every parathyroid gland has this appearance.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroidectomy as specified.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: An echogenic fatty hilum with centrally entering hilar vessels is a recognized sonographic lymph-node pattern that can help distinguish a nodule from a parathyroid candidate.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Single clinical review; the pattern is not an absolute exclusion rule and a node-like focus is not declared histologically benign.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroidectomy as specified.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: An inferior parathyroid gland not found in the expected lower-neck sites can be undescended near the carotid bifurcation or adjacent high neck.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Anatomical possibility, not a universal next-site priority; the revised case additionally supplies an imaging candidate.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroidectomy as specified.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: When operative exposure and imaging disagree, the remaining neck search should be correlated with the current localization observations rather than fixed to the initial projected site.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Clinical synthesis applied to the constructed observations, not a comparative trial of a universal search sequence. Histology and biochemical completeness remain separate.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroidectomy as specified.

I07_CLAIMS.statement: For the described arterial bifurcation, dividing the thyroid-bound limb after it separates from the parathyroid limb retains the latter inflow; dividing the common stem or entire bridge interrupts it.
I07_CLAIMS.limitation: Conditional application of the supplied vessel connections, not a measured probability or a claim that all parathyroid blood supply follows this pattern.
I07_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing cervical parathyroidectomy for sporadic PHPT or thyroidectomy as specified.

answerChoices.label: Explore the left thyrothymic tract and thymic tongue in the neck.
answerChoices.rationale: The unlocated tissue follows the inferior migration route. The thyrothymic region is the next directed search after the expected lower-pole site has been exposed.

answerChoices.label: Explore the left paraesophageal and retroesophageal tissue planes.
answerChoices.rationale: Posterior esophageal regions are credible ectopic sites, especially for superior glands. The identified superior gland and missing inferior gland make the thymic route the more appropriate next search here.

answerChoices.label: Explore the left thyroid lobe through a thyroidotomy.
answerChoices.rationale: An intrathyroidal gland is possible, but an empty lower-pole site does not establish that location. Ectopic search within the neck should precede a thyroid incision in this record.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Pediatric laryngospasm can produce inspiratory effort, paradoxical chest movement and absent airflow; complete closure may be silent.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Interpret with equipment and airway assessment; this pattern is not exclusive to one diagnosis.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Airway instrumentation in a child with an incompletely suppressed laryngeal reflex can provoke sustained glottic closure.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Mechanistic context, not an exact incidence or anesthesia-depth threshold.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Initial pediatric laryngospasm care includes stopping stimulation and oxygenation/airway maneuvers; IV propofol can deepen anesthesia when closure persists.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Suction or instrumentation can stimulate the larynx; this does not endorse repeated instrumentation of a closed airway.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: IV succinylcholine is a pediatric rescue option for persistent laryngospasm after initial measures and deeper anesthesia, with tracheal airway control as needed to restore ventilation.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The emergency item names IV succinylcholine without dose or timing. Contraindications and the complete rescue protocol require clinician review; no adult regimen is transferred.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Strong inspiratory effort against upper-airway obstruction can be followed by pulmonary edema after airway patency returns.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Recognized complication rather than an inevitable result or a probability; other pulmonary causes still require assessment.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Pink frothy tracheal secretions and persistent oxygenation difficulty after laryngospasm may require tracheal ventilation, PEEP and intensive-care escalation for pulmonary edema.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: SPA directly supports the treatment/disposition components; the independent review corroborates the mechanism. No PEEP level or universal intubation cutoff is claimed.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Pediatric peri-anesthetic bronchospasm can cause expiratory wheezing, higher airway pressure and an altered expiratory carbon-dioxide pattern.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Mechanical causes can resemble this pattern. No diagnostic sensitivity or numeric threshold is asserted.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Tube obstruction, including secretions, can resemble pediatric bronchospasm; assess tracheal-tube position and patency before attributing raised airway pressure to bronchoconstriction.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: One direct pediatric perioperative source independently verifies this specific diagnostic check in this ledger.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Inhaled albuterol is a pediatric acute bronchodilator option when bronchoconstriction is present and the airway permits drug delivery.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: No dose, puff count or redosing interval is authored. The case documents ongoing airflow and preserved circulation.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Severe or refractory pediatric bronchospasm may require systemic rescue; an exposure-related respiratory event with circulatory compromise changes the rescue priority.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: An absent rash does not exclude anaphylaxis. Ranking uses the full exposure/perfusion/ventilation course, not a single skin finding.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Dexamethasone is an anti-inflammatory corticosteroid adjunct in pediatric acute asthma; it does not replace prompt bronchodilation for current bronchoconstriction.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single-source support for this ranking boundary. Steroids may be appropriate adjuncts while rescue bronchodilation continues.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Intravenous magnesium is an escalation option for pediatric bronchospasm persisting despite initial bronchodilator treatment.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: No dose/rate is authored. The case has not yet received an inhaled beta agonist at the initial checkpoint.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Insufficient expiratory time during ventilation of a child with obstructed airways can cause air trapping, overexpansion and cardiovascular compromise.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single-source pediatric ICU-asthma support. Persistent flow at the next inspiration is an independently synthesized application of incomplete exhalation; intraoperative applicability needs clinician confirmation.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: With pediatric expiratory obstruction and air trapping, decrease respiratory frequency and allow longer exhalation instead of normalizing carbon dioxide with faster breaths.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single-source comparative support. Accept some hypercapnia with clinical monitoring; no exact rate, pressure, ratio, gas target or preferred ventilator mode is specified.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: External PEEP can improve airway patency or worsen hyperinflation in pediatric obstructive disease depending on physiology; it is not a universal correction for air trapping.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The source preserves competing approaches. No fixed asthma PEEP key or setting is scored; pulmonary-edema support is a separate context.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children aged 5-17 receiving anesthesia for supported procedures; exact synthetic profiles are ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: In pediatric acute bronchoconstriction, inhaled ipratropium is an adjunct to a short-acting beta agonist rather than a replacement for initial albuterol.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: This selects the first bronchodilator in the stated stable-delivery checkpoint; it does not prohibit combining agents for more severe disease.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Pediatric procedural anesthesia; the authored exact profiles remain ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: During time-cycled pressure-controlled ventilation, delivered tidal volume depends on the pressure target, inspiratory time and respiratory mechanics.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The item specifies mandatory time-triggered breaths and independently set inspiratory time. No mode superiority or exact pressure/time threshold is claimed.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Pediatric procedural anesthesia; the authored exact profiles remain ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: When inspiratory flow continues at time cycling in pressure control, shortening inspiration can further reduce the volume delivered during that breath.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Explicit physiologic application of the source-described pressure/time/volume relationship, not an empirical cutoff or universal prohibition. The constructed child already has reduced delivered volumes; ranking needs clinician review.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Pediatric procedural anesthesia; the authored exact profiles remain ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: With fixed inspiratory time, reducing mandatory breath frequency increases the time available for exhalation without shortening inspiration.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Mechanistic inference for the stated control mode, linked to directly pediatric obstructive-ventilation guidance. Ongoing gas exchange and circulation still need reassessment.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Pediatric procedural anesthesia; the authored exact profiles remain ages 7 and 12.

PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: After effective clearance of a currently patent tracheal airway, persistent pulmonary oxygenation difficulty with postobstructive edema findings calls for lung support rather than repeated airway clearance as the immediate priority.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Case-specific prioritization inferred from the pediatric airway-check and edema-support facts. Secretions that again obstruct the tube would change the immediate priority; clinician confirmation remains required.
PEDIATRIC_ANESTHESIA_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Pediatric procedural anesthesia; the authored exact profiles remain ages 7 and 12.

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Food impaction and solid-food dysphagia can be manifestations of pediatric EoE.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: The symptoms raise suspicion; they do not diagnose EoE or determine a sex/race-based selection weight.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Pediatric esophageal retrieval requires appropriate airway protection and a team equipped for the child.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: This packet supplies an established protected airway; it does not teach induction, intubation, dose rules or criteria for ASC credentialing.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Controlled piece-by-piece oral retrieval is an option for pediatric esophageal food-bolus clearance.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: The sources provide descriptive clearance guidance. In this item, actual successful retention and remaining enclosure access determine the offered strategy ranking, which requires pediatric endoscopist review.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: A pediatric food-bolus push maneuver requires a directly visualized distal esophageal lumen.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Single accessible pediatric procedural review directly supports this ranking boundary; do not infer that all push techniques are prohibited. The inaccessible 2026 paper is not used as corroboration.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: After pediatric food-bolus clearance, esophageal tissue sampling evaluates an underlying cause such as EoE.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Clinical safety can justify deferral; this constructed case has an established ongoing examination and no acquired contraindication. No universal biopsy-safety rate is asserted.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Pediatric EoE can have uneven esophageal involvement, so a distal collection does not represent other levels.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Distribution recommendations differ in detail; both support upper and lower sampling. No claim that a negative single level excludes disease.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Initial suspected childhood EoE assessment uses at least six esophageal biopsies distributed across levels.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: ESPGHAN supports at least six biopsies across upper and lower levels. SIGENP specifies two at each of three levels during initial evaluation. The offered plan adds two proximal and two middle biopsies to two recorded distal acquisitions, satisfying both approaches. This application concerns the constructed acquisition log.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: A visually smooth esophagus does not remove the need for appropriate biopsies when pediatric EoE is suspected.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: No frequency of normal endoscopy is encoded. Smooth appearance is a plausible stopping error, not a histologic result.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: PPI treatment can reduce diagnostic findings, so treatment before an incomplete initial tissue evaluation can complicate exclusion of EoE.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: No dose or washout interval is authored. The case is initially untreated; a child already receiving therapy needs a separately assessed plan.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Barium esophagram is recommended before pediatric EoE dilation when endoscopy cannot define the anatomy or caliber.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: The 2024 recommendation is direct. The 2025 practice point supports complementary luminal assessment, rather than an identical mandatory rule. No diameter, dilator size or fluoroscopy capability is invented.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Inflammatory tissue improvement does not establish that a persistent pediatric esophageal narrowing has resolved.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Histology and lumen answer different questions; the supplied observations do not prove a specific fibrotic mechanism.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Esophageal manometry evaluates motility rather than defining the extent of an endoscopically incompletely seen fixed narrowing.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Patient-specific ordering is a clinical application. Manometry can be appropriate for persistent symptoms after structural assessment; it is not categorically excluded from EoE care.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Repeating mucosal biopsies can reassess inflammation but does not map the full extent of an untraversed narrowing.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Existing samples remain valid within their stated territory; this is a distinction in the question answered, not a claim that repeat biopsy is never useful.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

I25_CLAIMS.statement: Swallowed topical corticosteroid treatment can improve histologic activity in pediatric EoE.
I25_CLAIMS.limitation: Budesonide appears as established historical care with documented response, not a newly prescribed regimen, treatment interval or escalation threshold.
I25_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children and adolescents; authored profiles limited to ages 5-17 with existing compatible child art

decisionNodes.stem: Which accessory should be used next to capture the disc during {patientName}'s esophageal retrieval?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: During {patientName}'s live esophageal coin retrieval, the scope views the coin's broad circular face. Its upper edge tilts toward the scope; its lower edge rests against the distal wall. Mucosa is visible through a gap behind the tilted segment. A gentle positioning check places the narrow grasper tips on opposite faces of that segment without mucosal tenting. The coin has not been withdrawn.

answerChoices.label: Capture with alligator forceps
answerChoices.rationale: A grasper is a reasonable candidate for this flat coin and the described direct-view positioning check. The check describes actual contact, rather than inferring access from a visible edge. A pediatric endoscopist must still confirm the device fit and ranking before this held exercise can be offered.

answerChoices.label: Capture with a retrieval net
answerChoices.rationale: A net may also retrieve a coin if it can deploy and retain the object. The recorded view does not prove that every enclosing device is unusable. This alternative remains a real technical competitor; no universal inferiority is asserted.

answerChoices.label: Capture with a polypectomy snare
answerChoices.rationale: A snare may capture a suitable segment when a stable loop can be established. The record does not include a snare trial and does not establish that the technique is impossible. Exact comparison with the grasper remains a clinical review hold.

decisionNodes.explanation: The revised record specifies the viewing direction, tilted segment and observed grasper contact. That makes the grasper a plausible candidate without repeating a keyed contact target in its label. It does not establish a difficult or independently validated accessory hierarchy. This once-revised exercise is parked pending pediatric endoscopist and educational-purpose review.

decisionNodes.stem: Which accessory should be used next to capture the marble during {patientName}'s gastric procedure?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: During {patientName}'s live gastric procedure, a solid glass marble moves freely in the gastric body. One gentle trial with a narrow grasper loses contact as the marble turns. The object has a continuous rounded surface without a projecting part.

answerChoices.label: Capture with a retrieval net
answerChoices.rationale: A net is a reasonable enclosure technique for a free rounded object. The available pediatric study supports its use but does not establish that it must outperform every basket or snare in this exact scene. This preference remains held for clinical ranking review.

answerChoices.label: Capture with a wire basket
answerChoices.rationale: A wire basket offers a genuinely different enclosing capture mechanism instead of repeating the failed narrow-grasper trial. Its ability to retain this object depends on the basket, object and withdrawal route. The current evidence does not prove it inferior here.

answerChoices.label: Capture with a polypectomy snare
answerChoices.rationale: A snare can provide a capture route for an object that remains inside its tightened loop. The single grasper failure does not test a snare or every forceps technique. A rounded object can be harder to retain, but the exact comparison is still unconfirmed.

decisionNodes.explanation: The recorded trial shows one unstable point contact, not failure of every forceps or snare technique. Net and basket enclosure are genuine alternatives. The revised candidate avoids the unchanged-repeat foil and the deployment-permission sentence, but the evidence does not settle a unique accessory preference. It is parked after one revision rather than presented as a hard resident item.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: When the vas and gonadal vessels continue through the deep ring, the operative search proceeds into the inguinal canal.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The guideline supplies the management rule; the independent regression series corroborates the anatomical category, not a randomized comparison of approaches.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: The vas and gonadal vessels can have different operative courses; the endpoint of the vas does not by itself establish the endpoint of the vessels.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Anatomical boundary, not a frequency estimate. Complete testicular-epididymal dissociation is uncommon and is not diagnosed solely from this fictional initial view.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: An apparent distal remnant without a demonstrated gonadal vascular endpoint is insufficient to conclude that the nonpalpable testis has been fully accounted for.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The guideline requires confident accounting for gonadal tissue, vas and vessels. Independent support concerns anatomical dissociation; exact next-step ranking still needs pediatric surgical review.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Persistent fibrous attachments and retroperitoneal vascular attachments can limit descent and may be mobilized before concluding that vessel-preserving orchiopexy is impossible.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Technique depends on safely identified anatomy and surgeon expertise. The independent cohort is younger than this art-supported population; no fixed dissection extent is prescribed.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Fowler-Stephens orchiopexy is an option when adequate scrotal reach cannot be achieved while retaining the gonadal vessels despite appropriate mobilization.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Does not rank one-stage versus two-stage Fowler-Stephens or traction techniques. Those competing strategies for persistent short vessels remain outside the scored packet.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A testis that reaches a scrotal pouch without cord tension can undergo primary orchiopexy with its gonadal vessels retained.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: No distance threshold, fixation method, guarantee of viability or success percentage is asserted. The independent series supports technique in a younger cohort.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Smaller testicular size is not equivalent to a fibrous remnant; a smaller but formed testis can be retained during orchiopexy.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: This is not an instruction to preserve a necrotic testis or a suspicious mass. The primary cohort retained hypotrophic testes, mostly in younger children; extrapolation to an older prepubertal child requires clinician confirmation.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Recommendations favoring removal of a small unilateral undescended testis in a postpubertal male should not be applied automatically to a prepubertal child.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Single eligible society guideline for this exact population boundary; no numerical puberty cutoff or mandatory operation for every adolescent is taught.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Damage to the gonadal vessels during orchiopexy can lead to testicular atrophy.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: General operative hazard; no exact probability, inevitable outcome or fertility prediction is asserted.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: Older society guidance allows stopping after confirmed blind-ended vas and vessels, while a later retrospective series found distal remnants despite that laparoscopic appearance.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: Withheld from scored teaching. A clinician must resolve whether additional distal exploration is appropriate; no inference about malignant transformation or viable whole testes is made from remnant histology.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Boys with an undescended/nonpalpable testis undergoing specialist exploration or orchiopexy; clinical age and anatomy require exact-version review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A specimen labelled as a testicular remnant must be assessed against its actual tissue and associated cord structures before it is used to conclude that gonadal tissue has been accounted for.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The society guideline supplies the incomplete-exploration management boundary; the regression series is a histology/anatomy cross-check. Absence of germ cells alone does not invalidate a genuine regressed testis, and no such rule is taught.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children undergoing specialist nonpalpable-testis exploration or orchiopexy; exact older-child anatomy and operative ranking require review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: A channel medial to the inferior epigastric vessels can shorten an angled route to the scrotum while retaining the gonadal vessels.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.limitation: The primary study describes a modified Prentiss channel that also preserves the epigastric vessels. No universal superiority, exact length gain, maximum age or obligatory step order is claimed; the fictional traction geometry determines the proposed ranking.
ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Children undergoing specialist nonpalpable-testis exploration or orchiopexy; exact older-child anatomy and operative ranking require review.

ORCHIOPEXY_INTRAOP_CLAIMS.statement: The descent passage must permit smooth testicular and cord passage; a restrictive passage is a different operative problem from a long or angled proximal route.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: During EMR, remaining macroscopic adenomatous tissue that is amenable to snare capture should be removed by snare before the resection is considered complete.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked multisociety publication; its snare-completion recommendation has low-quality supporting evidence. This does not rank bailout methods for a non-ensnarable remnant.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Surface thermal ablation is not a substitute for excision of visible adenoma that remains after snare resection.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline for the exact visible-remnant boundary. The offered remnant lifts and has not failed snare capture. No APC-versus-avulsion claim is made.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: After removal of all visible adenoma, adjunctive thermal treatment of the post-EMR mucosal margin can reduce local recurrence.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: Adjuvant treatment of a clear edge is a different task from destruction of visible residual tissue. No specific modality, generator setting, width or superiority comparison is taught.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: After EMR of a large nonpedunculated lesion in the right colon, prophylactic closure of a defect at least 20 mm across is supported when the edges can be approximated.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: USMSTF conditional recommendation with moderate-quality evidence; Singapore guidance supports selective high-risk/proximal closure. Not routine clipping of every polypectomy, and no benefit is guaranteed for an individual.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Prophylactic coagulation of nonbleeding visible vessels in a large EMR bed has not established the delayed-bleeding benefit of defect closure.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline reports a randomized trial without a significant reduction. This is not proof that coagulation never helps; it does not limit treatment of an actively bleeding vessel.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Mechanical clips and targeted endoscopic coagulation are accepted tools for intraprocedural polypectomy bleeding.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One guideline; conditional recommendation with low-quality evidence. There is no universal clip-versus-coagulation ranking for an uncomplicated bleeding point.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Large nonpedunculated colorectal lesions should be managed by an endoscopist experienced in advanced polypectomy.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline; capability.endoscopy by itself does not establish advanced EMR expertise or complication rescue support.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: A short stalk can fail to retain a detachable loop after polyp removal; observed loss of purchase can change the choice of mechanical hemostasis.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline summarizes device slippage with short stalks. The observed failed attempts, not a newly invented stalk-length threshold, select the alternative here. Exact clip capture requires clinician review.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Clips and detachable loops can compress pedunculated-polyp stalk vessels, and the achieved tissue capture matters when choosing between them.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: The Singapore detailed device comparison concerns prophylaxis; USMSTF also supports mechanical therapy for actual intraprocedural bleeding. The scored use after observed slippage is a scenario-specific application, not proof of general clip superiority.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: USMSTF describes dilute epinephrine as an optional adjunct to mechanical or coagulation treatment for intraprocedural bleeding.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One conditional guideline recommendation with low-quality evidence. No dose, concentration, duration, independent injection-monotherapy comparison or universal tool ranking is taught.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: An adenomatous epithelial surface can show a brown vascular network enclosing pale oval, tubular or branching structures and a browner appearance than surrounding mucosa.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline for the documented optical findings. Optical appearance is not histologic confirmation and this constructed written record does not measure image-reading skill.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: Submucosal injection dye highlights exposed submucosal fibers during colorectal EMR; a fibrous bed contour is distinct from a remaining epithelial surface.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly checked guideline describes differential staining and the submucosal plane. The combination of documented fibers and absence of epithelial openings is used here; blue color or elevation alone does not diagnose a remnant or injury.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: For a bleeding pedunculated-polyp stalk, expert technical guidance favors transverse clip capture at the stalk base to compress the feeder vessels.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One expert technical review for the exact placement rule, not a comparative efficacy trial. This supports a focused preferred-technique question, not a universal claim that another clip placement cannot work.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I14_CLAIMS.statement: For bleeding after sessile polyp removal, clip treatment aims to tamponade the underlying vessel, with opposing mucosal capture when feasible.
I14_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly read expert technical review. This is the counterfactual for a flat resection bed, not the target geometry of the offered projecting stalk.
I14_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly scoped therapeutic-colonoscopy scenarios; not an autonomous clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: A nonstructural pit pattern in a colorectal lesion raises concern for deep submucosal invasion.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Optical prediction is not histologic staging; the written constructed record tests interpretation of documented findings rather than actual image-reading skill.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: A nonpedunculated colorectal lesion with convincing optical features of deep invasion warrants tissue sampling and surgical evaluation rather than attempted endoscopic clearance.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Applies to convincing deep-invasion findings, not size or nonlifting after prior tattoo alone. Surgical evaluation is not an executed colectomy or a final cancer diagnosis.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: When sampling a suspicious colorectal lesion, the area with the concerning surface change is a more informative target than an ordinary-appearing peripheral area.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly accessed guideline for this precise sampling-target boundary. Sampling still cannot fully stage an unresected lesion.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: A superficial adenomatous biopsy does not exclude invasive disease elsewhere or deeper within a larger colorectal lesion.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly accessed primary statement for this sampling limitation. The scenario specifies the actual region and layers represented; no new sensitivity value is inferred.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: When endoscopic treatment of a lesion with suspected superficial invasion is appropriate, an intact resection supports pathological assessment better than fragmentation.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: This explains the closest endoscopic alternative, not an endorsement of ESD for the offered deep-invasion pattern or of advanced resection in an unconfirmed ASC capability.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: Expert piecemeal resection remains an option for selected large nonpedunculated lesions with benign optical features.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Counterfactual for the fragment-resection alternative; not permission to fragment a lesion with convincing invasive features. Local expertise and resources remain necessary.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: Keeping a resected polyp intact helps preserve the relationship between invasive tissue, stalk and excision margin for pathology.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly accessed source for the pedunculated specimen relationship. This is a specimen-quality principle, not a favorable-pathology or surveillance decision.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: Dividing a resected polyp during retrieval can undermine the anatomical assessment that an en-bloc excision was intended to preserve.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Application of documented intact-specimen and fragment-adequacy principles to retrieval. The net is the offered intact retrieval method, not a claim of superiority over every other intact device.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: A pedunculated polyp specimen can be prepared with its stalk extended and pinned before fixation to support subsequent oriented assessment.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Single older technical source; the society-hosted proof directly describes this step. No pin force, stretching distance, fixation concentration or duration is taught. Endoscopy-pathology local handling arrangements require confirmation.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: Pathology sections following the polyp head and stalk axis permit assessment of invasion relative to the stalk and resection end.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: One directly accessed source. Endoscopy staff orient and communicate; they do not replace the pathologist's sectioning protocol.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: Carbon marking at the site of a colorectal lesion can cause fibrosis that complicates later submucosal resection.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: A potential technical complication, not an inevitable outcome and not proof that a nonlifting lesion is cancer.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: BSG/ACPGBI guidance recommends separating a colorectal tattoo from a lesion by at least 30 mm to reduce interference with later endoscopic resection.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: One guideline and very-low-quality evidence for the exact distance. The proposed 4-cm anal-side site satisfies it; this item does not rank every remote oral-side site or establish a universal surgical tattoo convention.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

I15_CLAIMS.statement: The location of a colorectal marker must be communicated in relation to the lesion so a later procedural team can localize the intended site.
I15_CLAIMS.limitation: Local policies differ in marking number and surgical position. No universal number of injections, volume or surgical tattoo position is scored.
I15_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults at the explicitly constructed colonoscopy checkpoints; not a clinical-care protocol.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: A palpable laryngeal response to stimulation despite absent EMG directs troubleshooting toward the recording pathway.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: A recording-pathway problem includes electrode contact or circuitry; tube displacement is not proven until inspected.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: Residual neuromuscular blockade can suppress laryngeal EMG and must be considered when interpreting signal failure.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: No drug dose or quantitative recovery threshold is inferred; visible or palpable muscle responses help rank the available explanations.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: A stimulation-associated palpable laryngeal contraction shows that a motor response has occurred despite a missing displayed waveform.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: This is a technical localization clue, not proof of normal postoperative voice.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: A response near the laryngeal entry can persist when conduction fails farther proximally in the same recurrent nerve.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: Single adequate detailed society source for this exact localization boundary; current ATA guidance independently supports using proximal or vagal assessment.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: After the first lobectomy, ipsilateral vagal or proximal recurrent-nerve stimulation assesses the path before contralateral resection.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: ATA recommendation 23D is good-practice guidance; the independent observational methods corroborate the full-path checkpoint.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: An anatomically continuous recurrent nerve need not have preserved electrophysiologic conduction.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.limitation: Single adequate detailed source for the anatomy-versus-function distinction; visual inspection remains part of safe surgery.
INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing monitored thyroid surgery; extent decisions here concern noninvasive, clinically node-negative papillary thyroid cancers with normal baseline vocal-fold movement.

INTRAOP_I06_CLAIMS.statement: Persistent ipsilateral proximal response failure with preserved contralateral response after technical checks supports a true ipsilateral conduction problem.

decisionNodes.stem: During {patientName}'s paused open inguinal hernia repair, which drug should the anesthetist prioritize for the airway and circulatory deterioration while airway support and crystalloid resuscitation proceed?

answerChoices.label: Epinephrine
answerChoices.rationale: The exposure-linked combination of hypotension and bronchospasm supports treatment for perioperative anaphylaxis with epinephrine. A trained anesthetist titrates the IV preparation under monitoring.

answerChoices.label: Phenylephrine
answerChoices.rationale: A vasoconstrictor can raise pressure, but selecting routine anesthetic-hypotension treatment misses the concurrent bronchospasm and suspected systemic reaction. Epinephrine is the preferred initial rescue for that combination.

answerChoices.label: Albuterol
answerChoices.rationale: An inhaled bronchodilator can supplement care for bronchospasm, but it does not replace the systemic rescue needed for associated shock.

decisionNodes.stem: During {patientName}'s paused hernia repair, which ongoing IV vasoactive plan best fits the response at this reassessment while fluid resuscitation and emergency transfer arrangements continue?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The anesthetist has given titrated IV epinephrine boluses and crystalloid. Each bolus briefly restores blood pressure and pulse volume; both fall again between boluses. Wheezing eases. A pulse remains present, and monitored airway support continues.

answerChoices.label: Use continuous epinephrine
answerChoices.rationale: Repeated transient responses with recurrent poor perfusion support a titrated epinephrine infusion while fluid resuscitation and monitoring continue.

answerChoices.label: Use intermittent epinephrine
answerChoices.rationale: Boluses remain useful while an infusion is prepared, but repeatedly recurring compromise makes bolus-only delivery a less suitable ongoing strategy.

answerChoices.label: Use norepinephrine infusion
answerChoices.rationale: A second vasopressor is an escalation for shock persisting despite epinephrine infusion and fluids. The transient epinephrine responses here support establishing its sustained delivery first.

decisionNodes.explanation: The response recurs but does not last. Establish a monitored, titrated epinephrine infusion while continuing volume resuscitation. Boluses can bridge preparation; a second vasopressor becomes relevant if shock persists despite the infusion and fluids.

record.title: Sustained vasoactive support after transient epinephrine responses
fairness: The repeated restoration and loss of pressure/pulse volume supports a distinction between drug responsiveness and durable stabilization. Applying that distinction to the ongoing delivery plan favors a titrated epinephrine infusion over repeated intermittent rescue or moving directly to a different vasopressor. This is a consequential response interpretation followed by a treatment decision, with moderate predicted difficulty.

Continuous epinephrine is the defensible best offered ongoing strategy. The explanation preserves intermittent boluses as a bridge while preparing the infusion and recognizes a later role for a second vasopressor. No confident clinical inaccuracy or equally good ongoing alternative was identified in this offline review; an exact protocol or dose is not being tested.

'Each bolus briefly restores blood pressure and pulse volume; both fall again between boluses' is necessary response evidence, not an unfair wording cue. Removing it removes the reason to change delivery. Epinephrine appears in two choices and infusion/continuous delivery appears in two strategies, so a simple repeated-word match does not uniquely identify the key. No meaningful absolute, length outlier or teaching sentence supplies the answer before selection.

The current presentation correctly locates the exposure before incision and the crisis at the initial incision. Initial support, epinephrine boluses, reassessment and sustained support during transfer preparation follow coherently. The earlier explanation does not disclose the infusion decision. The shared presentation and this current update permit solving the node without remembering or selecting the preceding correct answer.

The task is complete and names the paused repair, ongoing IV plan, reassessment, fluids and transfer. The IV wording makes 'continuous epinephrine' understandable as an infusion. The adult demographics remain consistent, and there are no testing choices needing waits.

Temporary stabilization in an ASC while emergency transfer is arranged is plausible with appropriately trained anesthesia staff, monitoring and infusion resources. The scene does not imply that sustained shock is definitively managed at the ASC. This PASS concerns the current visible sequence and editorial decision quality, not actual resource admission or clinical approval.
suggestions: Preserve the repeated response-and-relapse observations, the bolus-bridge qualification and the distinction between establishing epinephrine delivery and later adding another vasopressor.

Keep the preceding feedback free of the infusion recommendation. Recheck the whole sequence if the introductory node is redesigned to meet the requested difficulty standard. No wording change to this node is required for this PASS.

record.title: Monica Hale: sustained support after transient epinephrine responses
fairness: The update supplies the decisive trajectory: IV epinephrine restores pressure and pulse volume, but the effect repeatedly does not persist; wheezing improves. fairness: The best offered plan is to retain the draining seton and defer definitive tract treatment. The learner must infer current rectal inflammatory activity from ulcers, friability and contact bleeding, then weigh it against the apparently favorable low posterior tract and preserved continence. That is a consequential two-step decision rather than a supplied diagnosis followed by a synonym.

Fistulotomy is a credible competing error because the tract is single, distal and associated with intact continence. The flap option represents choosing a sphincter-preserving operation while overlooking the condition of the rectal tissue. The current mucosal observations distinguish continued drainage from both immediate definitive procedures. No exact sphincter-division cutoff is needed to select the key here.

Known Crohn disease is legitimate management context, not disclosure of the requested decision. The exhibit supplies observed mucosal findings rather than the label active proctitis. The three options have comparable grammar and length. Keeping versus removing the seton is the clinical distinction being tested; the binary wording alone does not resolve it without interpreting the case.

The examination is live and its decision-critical observations are explicitly visible in text. A stable adult with a functioning seton undergoing EUA and possible tract treatment is plausible in an ambulatory OR. Mara Ellison's age and sex are supplied, and the task identifies her current EUA. No pediatric restrictions apply.

This first checkpoint stands alone. Its explanation addresses rectal activity and staging, without teaching the later biopsy answer. The subsequent node describes continuing examination and makes the earlier plan provisional; on the keyed path there is no irreversible operation before the later tissue finding. Do not interpret this PASS as permission to execute a definitive procedure before completing the examination.

High yield: selection and timing of fistula treatment in Crohn disease, including why favorable anatomy does not erase active rectal disease. Predicted moderate, not hard: the new mucosal finding is recognizable, but it must defeat a clinically attractive anatomical plan.

No confident clinical inaccuracy or equally defensible competing key was identified from the supplied candidate fields. This PASS is editorial and does not constitute new source verification or named clinician approval.
suggestions: Preserve this exact candidate wording and its observed mucosal findings. Keep the distinction between temporary staging and indefinite seton treatment in the explanation.

When presenting the paired case, retain this checkpoint's available information and show the subsequent examination update before any later diagnostic decision. Preserve the explicit provisional-plan chronology.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After right jugular access, the catheter descends along the right mediastinal border on the frontal view. The lateral view places its lower segment immediately behind the sternum. A gentle hand-injected completion study outlines a narrow descending parasternal vein around that segment; the brachiocephalic vein and SVC fill without a narrowing, and contrast remains intravascular. Blood can be aspirated from the catheter.
decisionNodes.stem: Which catheter maneuver should be selected before completing Priya's port implantation on these views?

answerChoices.label: Withdraw the catheter to its branch point and redirect centrally
answerChoices.rationale: The anterior parasternal course identifies a tributary rather than a catheter descending within the SVC. Patent central veins and an intravascular route support withdrawing from the tributary and redirecting under the ongoing imaging.

answerChoices.label: Advance the catheter along its current course to the intended depth
answerChoices.rationale: Advancing changes length within the same anterior tributary; it does not turn that route into the patent SVC. Successful aspiration confirms access to blood, not the intended central course.

answerChoices.label: Remove the current catheter and establish contralateral jugular access
answerChoices.rationale: A new puncture may be needed when the central route is obstructed or cannot be corrected. The present study demonstrates a patent central confluence, so the available route can first be redirected.

decisionNodes.explanation: The frontal projection is misleading: the anterior parasternal course fits the internal thoracic venous route rather than the SVC. Intravascular contrast and blood return do not establish a suitable long-term central position. With a patent central confluence, withdraw from the tributary and redirect under imaging before completing the port. This does not prescribe an exact tip-to-carina distance or routine high-right-atrial placement.

record.title: Correct an anterior parasternal port-catheter course
fairness: The described frontal, lateral and contrast findings permit recognition of a tributary course rather than satisfactory central placement. Preserved aspiration and intravascular contrast do not settle suitability for use. The patent central route then supports redirection through the existing access rather than choosing new contralateral access.

The alternatives answer the same immediate catheter-management task. Advancement along the described tributary is not a suitable correction; starting over contralaterally is a possible fallback but is not the best first maneuver when the current central route is patent and no failed redirection is described. Exactly one best answer is defensible among these options.

The two reasoning steps are consequential: interpret the discordant projections, then select a correction that uses the demonstrated patent route. The right-sided frontal course and blood return provide credible reasons to underestimate the malposition. Difficulty is moderate, not hard.

No strong nonmedical wording overlap, length outlier, convergence, absolute or pre-answer diagnosis label identifies the key. The patency finding is necessary decision information rather than gratuitous permission to choose the key.

Port placement with completion fluoroscopy/contrast and appropriate access expertise is plausible in an equipped ASC. The scene shows those imaging resources being used; it does not require live hospital reconstruction. Imaging before acceptance for use is coherent, and this standalone task supplies the named adult and procedural stage.

The high-yield construct is recognizing and correcting central-catheter malposition despite blood return. Memorizing this particular internal thoracic tributary route is more specialized and should not be represented as independently established common exam content.

No definite anatomical or management inaccuracy identified offline. This is an editorial PASS of the displayed decision, not verification of source currency, runtime capability admission or named clinician approval.
suggestions: Optional presentation improvement: say 'the described views' or supply a labeled, independently constructed two-view schematic. The existing written observations are sufficient to solve the item, but an image would let residents inspect the spatial relationship directly.

Optional precision improvement: make imaging-guided redirection explicit in the choice, consistent with the existing explanation. Do not imply blind advancement or add an unsupported exact tip-depth target.
Any clinical-content revision should retain the patent-route and intravascular findings that distinguish correction from starting a new access, and should receive exact-version review.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old woman, is undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the clinic's ambulatory OR. The arterial branch entering the gallbladder has been clipped and divided. A clip is across the gallbladder end of the presumed cystic duct; a small opening has been made just below that clip for a catheter. This duct has not been divided across or clipped on its common-duct side. Fluoroscopy and near-infrared imaging are available; ICG was given at induction.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Irrigation clears the field, but green fluid collects again medial to the gallbladder neck, away from the small duct opening. The gallbladder wall is unbroken. The duct opening is visible, accepts a fine catheter without traction and remains accessible below the gallbladder-side clip.
decisionNodes.stem: Which mapping approach should be used for {patientName}'s recurrent bile at this laparoscopic cholecystectomy checkpoint?

answerChoices.label: Acquire a transcystic contrast cholangiogram using fluoroscopy
answerChoices.rationale: The accessible opening is below the clip and permits contrast to enter the ductal tree. Recurrent bile outside the unbroken gallbladder calls for assessment of the lumen and any escape of contrast.

answerChoices.label: Acquire a gallbladder-injection contrast cholangiogram using fluoroscopy
answerChoices.rationale: Gallbladder injection is an operative cholangiography route when it communicates with the ducts. At this checkpoint the clip closes that outlet; filling the gallbladder would not provide the intended ductal study.

answerChoices.label: Acquire a fluorescence cholangiogram using near-infrared imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Fluorescence is useful for anatomical orientation, and ICG is already available in the bile. It does not replace the selected contrast study of the ductal lumen and extravasation in this new-bile assessment. The guideline preference is conditional, not a universal prohibition on fluorescence.

decisionNodes.explanation: Recurrent bile outside an unbroken gallbladder changes the imaging objective from orientation to assessment of a possible duct leak. Contrast can enter the ducts through the accessible opening below the clip; injection into the gallbladder would encounter the closed outlet. Fluorescence remains a useful adjunct, but the proposed contrast study defines luminal continuity and contrast escape. This checkpoint does not establish an injury class or its treatment.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At the next checkpoint, the catheter has been removed. Suction and gentle retraction bring two open duct ends into view within the existing dissection field. Circulation remains stable and laparoscopic exposure permits drainage. The operating surgeon does not perform biliary reconstruction. The acquisition record is shown below.
decisionNodes.stem: Which immediate plan should be selected for {patientName} after these findings during laparoscopic cholecystectomy?

answerChoices.label: Drain the subhepatic space and arrange hepatobiliary-center transfer
answerChoices.rationale: These acquisitions connect the intrahepatic system and papilla to different open ends in the field. With bile control achievable and no local reconstructive expertise, drainage and hepatobiliary-center transfer provide the appropriate immediate bridge to specialist treatment.

answerChoices.label: Drain the subhepatic space and request transpapillary stenting
answerChoices.rationale: A routine transpapillary stent diverts a communicating leak through the distal outlet. Here the upper study fills both hepatic ducts without reaching that outlet, while the lower study reaches the duodenum without filling the hepatic system. Ordinary stenting alone does not reconnect them; specialist combined techniques are a separate question.

answerChoices.label: Drain the subhepatic space and dissect proximally to expose the hepatic confluence
answerChoices.rationale: The complementary studies already show the hepatic system and distal outlet opening separately. Further proximal dissection for a more complete injury description can compromise tissue needed by the receiving specialist. This differs from gaining exposure or control when either is inadequate.

decisionNodes.explanation: The decisive finding is the combination of the two injection origins and their separate hepatic versus duodenal connections, together with the visible open ends. Escape around an injected opening alone could be reflux and would not establish this pattern. Routine papillary diversion would address the distal system but not restore the absent connection to the hepatic ducts. Drain and arrange specialist transfer within the stated expertise limit. Further proximal dissection solely to complete a local injury description is unnecessary here; conversion remains appropriate when required for exposure or control. Repair timing and method belong to the HPB team.
