concepts.learningObjective: Use a structured multidimensional frailty assessment rather than inferring frailty from age or comorbidity before elective major abdominal surgery.

concepts.displayName: Plan multicomponent delirium prevention
concepts.learningObjective: Communicate a tailored nonpharmacologic multicomponent prevention plan to the hospital perioperative team for an at-risk adult.

concepts.displayName: Apply USPSTF annual LDCT eligibility
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the USPSTF age, smoking-exposure, quit-interval, and treatment-fitness framework for external annual LDCT referral.

concepts.displayName: Discuss PSP recurrence-prevention referral
concepts.learningObjective: Offer conditional thoracic-surgery discussion after initial primary spontaneous pneumothorax when recurrence prevention matters to the patient.

concepts.displayName: Refer high-risk pleural infection for drainage
concepts.learningObjective: Use the complete low-pH pleural-infection context to arrange hospital drainage rather than outpatient delay.

concepts.displayName: Refer for image-guided thoracentesis
concepts.learningObjective: Refer an indicated diagnostic thoracentesis for image guidance rather than a blind clinic procedure.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish ionizing imaging modalities
concepts.learningObjective: Explain CT's ionizing X-ray exposure versus the nonionizing mechanisms of ultrasound and MRI during patient-specific imaging counseling.

concepts.displayName: Verify an implant's MRI conditions
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the exact implanted device and arrange MRI-team verification of device-specific conditions before clearance for the proposed scan.

concepts.displayName: Classify a contrast event
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish isolated transient iodinated-contrast warmth from urticaria when reviewing a fully documented outside contrast event.

concepts.displayName: Recognize SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis
concepts.learningObjective: Link SGLT2 exposure to ketoacidosis when compatible ketone/acidosis evidence is supplied despite nonmarked glucose elevation.

concepts.displayName: Explain naloxone's receptor action
concepts.learningObjective: Explain competitive opioid receptor antagonism in patient-specific naloxone counseling or review of completed emergency care.

concepts.displayName: Plan drug-specific SGLT2 interruption
concepts.learningObjective: Use drug-specific U.S. labeling to plan elective preoperative interruption of empagliflozin versus ertugliflozin without assigning every SGLT2 inhibitor one interval.

concepts.displayName: Explain absorbed laparoscopic CO2
concepts.learningObjective: Explain the extra blood CO2 load and potential respiratory acidemia from peritoneal absorption of insufflated CO2 when reviewing a completed outside laparoscopic operation.

concepts.displayName: Interpret pneumoperitoneum venous return
concepts.learningObjective: Explain pressure-associated venous compression while accounting for position and phase instead of assuming pneumoperitoneum always changes preload in one direction.

concepts.displayName: Explain reassuring referred shoulder pain
concepts.learningObjective: Explain a diaphragmatic/phrenic contributor to mild improving shoulder pain after laparoscopy only when current assessment is reassuring and warning features remain explicit.

concepts.displayName: Explain wound collagen remodeling
concepts.learningObjective: Explain the shift from relatively type III-rich early wound matrix toward type I collagen during remodeling in patient-specific scar counseling.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish raised scars by their boundary
concepts.learningObjective: Use extension beyond versus confinement within the original wound to distinguish a keloid from a hypertrophic scar.

concepts.displayName: Recognize secondary-intention healing
concepts.learningObjective: Identify a clinician-selected open wound healing without immediate or planned delayed edge approximation as secondary-intention healing.

concepts.displayName: Explain an IgE-mediated type I reaction
concepts.learningObjective: Connect a documented IgE-mediated type I reaction to mast-cell activation rather than infer the mechanism from a rash alone.

concepts.displayName: Explain allergic contact dermatitis
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize specialist-confirmed allergic contact dermatitis as T-cell-mediated type IV hypersensitivity and distinguish it from an IgE reaction.

concepts.displayName: Explain documented hyperacute graft rejection
concepts.learningObjective: Identify pre-existing recipient donor-reactive antibodies and vascular injury as the mechanism in an outside-confirmed historical hyperacute allograft event.

concepts.displayName: Choose a conditional aPTT mixing assessment
concepts.learningObjective: Select a specialist mixing study as an initial deficiency-versus-inhibition assessment for a repeated unexplained isolated prolonged aPTT when immediate FVIII:C is unavailable and interferences have been assessed.

concepts.displayName: Interpret a mixing study as an initial clue
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret correction, noncorrection and time-dependent changes as initial laboratory clues while preserving method limitations and the need for factor/inhibitor assessment.

concepts.displayName: Separate cancer stage from tumor grade
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish cancer-specific anatomic extent from microscopic differentiation without treating either as a universal numeric scheme or prognosis.

concepts.displayName: Explain classic biallelic RB1 loss
concepts.learningObjective: Explain an explicitly documented loss of both functioning RB1 alleles as a classic tumor-suppressor loss mechanism without generalizing it to every gene or inferring inherited disease.

concepts.displayName: Classify operative contamination conditions
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish clean, clean-contaminated, contaminated and dirty/infected operative wound classes using the described tract entry, spillage and pre-existing infection.

concepts.displayName: Check pregnancy in pelvic-pain assessment
concepts.learningObjective: Select pregnancy hCG testing during assessment of reproductive-age pelvic or abdominal pain when pregnancy is possible.

concepts.displayName: Escalate a suspected ectopic pregnancy
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize symptomatic possible ectopic pregnancy and arrange urgent specialist-capable assessment despite initial hemodynamic stability.

concepts.displayName: Localize median compression at the wrist
concepts.learningObjective: Use supplied sensory distribution and wrist findings to localize a carpal-tunnel pattern to the median nerve at the wrist.

concepts.displayName: Localize ulnar compression at the elbow
concepts.learningObjective: Use supplied little/ring-finger symptoms and elbow provocation to localize cubital-tunnel compression to the ulnar nerve at the elbow.

concepts.displayName: Evaluate a persistent adult neck mass
concepts.learningObjective: Continue malignancy evaluation of a persistent adult lateral/cystic mass with an appropriate selected contrast-enhanced neck CT, without reassurance from cystic appearance.

concepts.displayName: Refer for initial needle sampling of a neck mass
concepts.learningObjective: Choose specialist fine-needle aspiration as the best offered initial needle approach for an assessed at-risk adult neck mass rather than initial open biopsy.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish a graft from a flap by blood supply
concepts.learningObjective: Classify supplied reconstructive tissue transfers by whether blood supply is retained or carried and reconnected, rather than by donor identity or location.

concepts.displayName: Explain epithelial regrowth at a split-thickness donor site
concepts.learningObjective: Explain how retained donor-site skin appendage epithelium contributes to resurfacing after a split-thickness harvest, separately from recipient-graft vascularization.

concepts.displayName: Classify graft donor relationships
concepts.learningObjective: Classify an autograft, allograft, isograft or xenograft from the supplied donor-recipient relationship.

concepts.displayName: Explain local-anesthetic nerve blockade
concepts.learningObjective: Identify voltage-gated sodium-channel blockade as the principal mechanism interrupting sensory nerve excitation and conduction.

concepts.displayName: Explain tacrolimus immunosuppression
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the FKBP12–calcineurin pathway and suppression of T-cell activation underlying tacrolimus immunosuppression.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish paralysis from anesthesia
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize that neuromuscular blockade produces skeletal-muscle relaxation without itself providing unconsciousness or analgesia.

concepts.displayName: Recognize systemic local-anesthetic toxicity
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize a compatible neurologic or cardiac toxicity pattern after supplied local-anesthetic exposure in a completed outside-care event.

concepts.displayName: Explain refeeding-related phosphate shifts
concepts.learningObjective: Explain how carbohydrate-associated insulin and the return to anabolic metabolism can lower serum phosphate through cellular uptake in a compatible refeeding course.

concepts.displayName: Plan thiamine in high-risk nutrition restart
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize planned thiamine before a specialist-monitored high-risk nutrition restart, while retaining separate electrolyte and clinical monitoring.

concepts.displayName: Match RCA and FMEA to the safety task
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish retrospective event-centered root cause analysis from prospective process-centered healthcare failure mode and effects analysis.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish saturation from oxygen content
concepts.learningObjective: Explain why a normal oxygen saturation does not establish adequate hemoglobin-dependent oxygen content or exclude supplied anemia.

concepts.displayName: Attribute bowel melanoma to its confirmed skin primary
concepts.learningObjective: Use a supplied cutaneous primary and confirmatory outside pathology to identify small-bowel melanoma as metastatic disease retaining the primary cancer's identity.

concepts.displayName: Interpret negative films after swallowing a bone
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize that negative plain films and preserved breathing do not exclude a retained swallowed bone in a symptomatic esophageal context.

concepts.displayName: Refer confirmed sharp esophageal objects emergently
concepts.learningObjective: Arrange emergency hospital therapeutic endoscopic care for a confirmed sharp esophageal foreign body rather than elective observation or routine clinic scheduling.

concepts.displayName: Perioperative ART continuity
concepts.learningObjective: Plan continued antiretroviral treatment when feasible and coordinate unavoidable interruptions with the HIV team.

concepts.displayName: Boosted ART and midazolam
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize increased midazolam exposure with ritonavir or cobicistat and coordinate route-specific sedation planning.

concepts.displayName: Quantitative blockade recovery assessment
concepts.learningObjective: Use quantitative neuromuscular monitoring rather than head lift, apparent strength or visual twitch count alone to assess recovery from blockade.

concepts.displayName: Sugammadex pharmacologic selectivity
concepts.learningObjective: Identify rocuronium and vecuronium as the blockers selectively complexed by sugammadex rather than assuming universal relaxant reversal.

concepts.displayName: Effluent-associated irritant dermatitis
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize peristomal irritant injury by the leakage distribution and distinguish it from an infectious or ulcerative process.

concepts.displayName: Correct the leaking ostomy seal
concepts.learningObjective: Address noninfectious leakage-related dermatitis with appliance fit, a compatible skin-protection plan and ostomy-nurse follow-up.

concepts.displayName: Stoma mucocutaneous separation
concepts.learningObjective: Identify detachment at the sutured intestinal mucosa-to-skin junction rather than labeling every stoma wound as retraction or necrosis.

concepts.displayName: Care of limited superficial stoma separation
concepts.learningObjective: Choose local ostomy care and close follow-up for small superficial separation with viable bowel, while reserving surgical escalation for complicated separation.

concepts.displayName: Gallbladder lamina-propria invasion
concepts.learningObjective: Identify gallbladder carcinoma confined to the lamina propria as T1a, distinguishing muscular invasion from in-situ disease.

concepts.displayName: Completely resected incidental T1a gallbladder cancer
concepts.learningObjective: Avoid automatic radical re-resection after expert confirmation of completely removed margin-negative T1a gallbladder carcinoma.

concepts.displayName: Cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma recognition
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize Merkel cell carcinoma from an integrated cutaneous neuroendocrine pathology assessment rather than assuming every skin nodule is squamous cancer.

concepts.displayName: Merkel sentinel-node staging
concepts.learningObjective: Refer an appropriate clinically node-negative Merkel cell carcinoma candidate for sentinel-node staging rather than equating a normal node examination with pathologic node negativity.

concepts.displayName: Retrorectus mesh plane
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the retrorectus mesh plane between rectus muscle and posterior rectus sheath in midline incisional hernia planning.

concepts.displayName: Fascial closure rather than mesh bridging
concepts.learningObjective: Plan fascial-defect closure with mesh reinforcement in an elective midline incisional hernia expected to close without advanced release, rather than routine bridging.

concepts.displayName: Subtotal bailout in unsafe anatomy
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize subtotal cholecystectomy as a safe bailout option when the critical view cannot be obtained rather than dividing unidentified structures.

concepts.displayName: Subtotal remnant classification
concepts.learningObjective: Classify subtotal cholecystectomy as fenestrating or reconstituting according to whether the remaining gallbladder is left open or closed.

concepts.displayName: Insufflation CO2 absorption
concepts.learningObjective: Explain a documented gradual CO2 rise during uncomplicated pneumoperitoneum by systemic absorption of insufflated gas rather than assuming an unrelated acute catastrophe.

concepts.displayName: Pneumoperitoneum and respiratory compliance
concepts.learningObjective: Relate increased airway pressure during evaluated pneumoperitoneum to cephalad diaphragm displacement and reduced respiratory compliance.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative spinal accessory localization
concepts.learningObjective: Localize weak shoulder shrug and trapezius-pattern shoulder droop after posterior-triangle neck surgery to spinal accessory injury.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative long thoracic localization
concepts.learningObjective: Localize medial scapular winging on forward pushing after axillary surgery to the long thoracic nerve and serratus anterior.

concepts.displayName: Refer a childhood inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Refer a clinically suspected childhood inguinal hernia for pediatric surgical assessment rather than applying adult observation criteria.

concepts.displayName: Observe uncomplicated childhood neck nodes
concepts.learningObjective: Choose observation with reassurance and safety-net advice for a well child with small mobile cervical nodes and no concerning findings.

concepts.displayName: Refer concerning childhood neck nodes
concepts.learningObjective: Arrange early pediatric assessment of a concerning cervical-node pattern without assigning a cancer diagnosis from a red flag alone.

concepts.displayName: Refer suspected acquired testicular ascent
concepts.learningObjective: Refer a previously scrotal testis that no longer maintains a normal scrotal position for pediatric specialist assessment.

concepts.displayName: Follow a true retractile testis
concepts.learningObjective: Choose documented position surveillance for a true retractile testis and reassess or refer if it acquires a persistently higher position.

concepts.displayName: Evaluate symptomatic pectus excavatum
concepts.learningObjective: Refer a stable adolescent with pectus excavatum and exertional symptoms for specialist evaluation before attributing the symptoms or choosing corrective treatment.

concepts.displayName: Discuss brace assessment for pectus carinatum
concepts.learningObjective: Offer specialist brace-suitability assessment to a young person with pectus carinatum seeking active nonsurgical care, without promising a universal regimen or outcome.

concepts.displayName: Plan conservative adolescent pilonidal care
concepts.learningObjective: Discuss individualized conservative care and reassessment for limited adolescent pilonidal disease without an acute abscess, rather than selecting an operation by default.

concepts.displayName: Include the child in a nonurgent care discussion
concepts.learningObjective: Explain a nonurgent clinic plan to the child at an appropriate level, invite questions and seek developmentally appropriate assent while involving the parent.

concepts.displayName: Recognize rectus diastasis
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a supplied broad rectus-separation pattern from a focal abdominal-wall hernia without assuming that the conditions cannot coexist.

concepts.displayName: Recognize an epidermoid cyst
concepts.learningObjective: Select epidermoid cyst as the best clinical fit for a slowly growing cutaneous lump with a central punctum, without claiming histologic certainty.

concepts.displayName: Recognize an external hemorrhoid clot
concepts.learningObjective: Identify a clot-filled painful external anal-margin lump as a thrombosed external hemorrhoid rather than internal prolapse or another proposed anal lesion.

concepts.displayName: Counsel gentle care for anal itching
concepts.learningObjective: Choose gentle cleansing and drying for assessed uncomplicated perianal irritation while avoiding abrasive or fragranced care and retaining reassessment.

concepts.displayName: Complete an inadequately prepared colonoscopy
concepts.learningObjective: Select an adequately prepared repeat colonoscopy when the whole-colon examination cannot support the intended assessment, with review of preparation failure rather than a fixed repeat timetable.

concepts.displayName: Choose cold snare for a small colorectal polyp
concepts.learningObjective: Choose cold snare for a supplied accessible 4 mm or 7 mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyp without invasive features in an outside endoscopic removal plan.

concepts.displayName: Plan surveillance for nondysplastic Barrett
concepts.learningObjective: Select endoscopic surveillance rather than prophylactic eradication for established nondysplastic Barrett in a suitable patient without a visible neoplastic lesion.

concepts.displayName: Arrange adult support after endoscopic sedation
concepts.learningObjective: Plan responsible adult collection and support after sedated gastroscopy rather than self-driving or unaccompanied travel and recovery.

concepts.displayName: Clarify a preoperative penicillin label
concepts.learningObjective: Obtain a structured reaction history before selecting testing, referral or a record change for an incompletely characterized penicillin-allergy label before ASC care.

concepts.displayName: Plan appropriate surgical hair preparation
concepts.learningObjective: Leave noninterfering surgical-site hair alone and select clippers when removal is needed for a supplied non-genital ambulatory operative field.

concepts.displayName: Apply benzodiazepine-antagonist contraindication after seizure control
concepts.learningObjective: Use the actual indication for perioperative midazolam to choose a reversal plan when supported respiratory depression competes with preservation of treatment for a potentially life-threatening seizure state.

concepts.displayName: Resolve technical and symptom-protocol limitations in motility testing
concepts.learningObjective: Assess whether an existing esophageal pressure study answers the clinical question and select completion, assisted placement or provocative testing before disease-specific treatment.

concepts.displayName: Resolve occult-groin imaging and symptom discordance
concepts.learningObjective: Choose an adequate targeted repeat study or dynamic cross-sectional assessment by interpreting prior scan localization, provocation, symptom reproduction and competing musculoskeletal findings.

concepts.displayName: Apply symptom attribution to a demonstrated inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish hernia-related from coexisting musculoskeletal pain and select a repair discussion or observation without assuming every positive image explains the patient's limitation.

concepts.displayName: Resolve cystic thyroid-node imaging/cytology discordance
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted tissue confirmation for a suspicious cervical node when prior fluid-only aspiration does not explain its solid imaging features, before determining operative nodal management.

concepts.displayName: Resolve partial skin-biopsy and microstaging limitations
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a representative diagnostic completion strategy when specimen location, deep transection or clinicopathologic discordance prevents a reliable whole-lesion diagnosis or microstage before definitive reconstruction/staging.

concepts.displayName: Apply regional-node evidence before sentinel staging
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a clinically node-negative melanoma basin from a proven-positive or suspicious nonrepresentatively sampled node, and choose the appropriate next diagnostic/staging pathway.

concepts.displayName: Complete colon staging from actual prior imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Retain adequate prior staging while selecting targeted characterization or missing-region imaging from the actual coverage and unresolved findings of outside examinations.

concepts.displayName: Assess local MRI adequacy before soft-tissue biopsy
concepts.learningObjective: Choose completion of local MRI based on the actual field coverage, compartment mapping and viable-target information missing from an outside study before biopsy planning.

concepts.displayName: Reconcile mucosal sampling with a characteristic subepithelial lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret whether a negative surface specimen samples the EUS-defined layer and decide whether a characteristic colonic lipoma needs further tissue confirmation.

concepts.displayName: Choose gastric MALT care from post-eradication trajectory
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish regressing asymptomatic residual gastric MALT or molecular persistence from progressive symptomatic disease after interpretable infection reassessment, and choose monitoring versus escalation.

concepts.displayName: Apply gastric lymphoma morphology to the treatment pathway
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate gastric small-cell architecture, molecular-test limitations and the actual distribution of large cells before selecting an indolent MALT rather than aggressive/reactive care pathway.

concepts.displayName: Apply uncertainty to a target-benefit decision
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate an effect estimate, confidence interval and null test to distinguish target benefit confirmed, excluded or unresolved and avoid false adoption, futility or equivalence conclusions.

concepts.displayName: Apply vascular, contents and duct findings to collection treatment
concepts.learningObjective: Choose the route and sequence of intervention for a clinically consequential post-pancreatitis collection by interpreting arterial findings, necrotic contents and partial versus complete duct interruption.

concepts.displayName: Complete collection imaging for a specific intervention question
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted vascular, internal-content or pancreatic-duct assessment from actual prior imaging and clinical findings before choosing a collection intervention.

concepts.displayName: Resolve breast imaging/core-biopsy discordance
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret target position and specimen contents after a benign breast core result and choose representative further tissue assessment rather than dismiss a persistent suspicious parenchymal lesion.

concepts.displayName: Sequence treatment of recurrent ulcer bleeding
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish recurrent bleeding after initially successful endoscopy from failure of repeat hemostasis and select repeat endoscopy, angiographic or operative rescue from actual resuscitation/access findings.

concepts.displayName: Recognize failed repeat ulcer hemostasis and select rescue
concepts.learningObjective: Use documented repeat-endoscopy failure and target access to choose angiographic versus further endoscopic or operative rescue for recurrent peptic-ulcer bleeding.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish clinical characterization from histologic confirmation
concepts.learningObjective: Use the EUS-defined lesion layer and the actual submitted tissue to document whether a clinically characterized fatty submucosal lesion has histologic confirmation, without equating that status with a need for another biopsy.

concepts.displayName: Interpret provocative motility responses before further planning
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish post-rapid-swallow contractile reserve from liquid-load outflow findings using actual pressure responses, without converting a provocative finding into a complete motor diagnosis.

concepts.displayName: Interpret mapped partial specimens before melanoma planning
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate the specimen's location, represented tissue compartments and cut surface to retain valid local findings while limiting whole-lesion diagnosis or depth claims before completion pathology.

concepts.displayName: Integrate enhancement and compartment anatomy in biopsy planning
concepts.learningObjective: Use matched precontrast/postcontrast findings and compartment relationships to select a viable proposed target and tract for the radiology planning report.

concepts.displayName: Prioritize care when groin findings have competing symptom sources
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate interval functional observations with a demonstrated reducible inguinal hernia and coexisting musculoskeletal findings to choose the current care priority.

concepts.displayName: Select diagnostic extent after a locally in-situ partial specimen
concepts.learningObjective: Apply an adequately described local epidermal melanoma finding to the next primary-site procedure without extending that finding to an unrepresented raised residual component.

concepts.displayName: Integrate partial depth records before a nodal-staging discussion
concepts.learningObjective: Preserve demonstrated invasive depth across mapped partial specimens and decide whether that evidence already supports a sentinel-node staging discussion while primary assessment continues.

concepts.displayName: Check MRI acquisition comparability before biopsy targeting
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize when different acquisition settings prevent an intrinsically bright mass region from being assessed for contrast-related signal change, and request the comparison needed before targeting.

concepts.displayName: Target an axial superficial-reflux referral
concepts.learningObjective: Use duplex anatomy to identify the axial superficial-vein target for specialist intervention assessment.

concepts.displayName: DCIS axillary staging at mastectomy
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the planned mastectomy setting to choose the timing and extent of axillary staging for sampled DCIS.

concepts.displayName: Apply final DCIS cavity-margin findings
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile oriented main and additional cavity specimens, then apply the pure-DCIS margin rule to the final treatment decision.

concepts.displayName: Plan imaging after a changed postlaparoscopy course
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret the postoperative course, then distinguish biliary leak detection from duct-anatomy localization in a stable CT-assessed record.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish reflux assessment from DVT imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a completed compression-only venous study, then select the diagnostic protocol needed for symptomatic superficial venous treatment assessment.

concepts.displayName: Interpret treatment response in hyperkalaemia
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish ECG stabilization from potassium correction and select the remaining treatment mechanism in a completed inpatient record.

concepts.displayName: Act on an unrepresentative adult neck aspirate
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a cyst-fluid specimen in a persistent adult neck lesion and request representative needle reassessment rather than presume benignity or jump to open surgery.

concepts.displayName: Apply new decompensation findings to elective planning
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret new fluid findings despite reassuring biochemical results and select optimization before a nonurgent operation.

concepts.displayName: Select source imaging in a lymphangitic presentation
concepts.learningObjective: Localize a distal source from the proximal lymphatic pattern, then choose imaging of an uncertain source swelling rather than the tender veins or draining nodes.

concepts.displayName: Interpret a paired pressure challenge
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate controlled circulatory observations with ventilator-pressure observations to distinguish venous-return and respiratory-mechanics explanations.

concepts.displayName: Apply an agreed perioperative directive endpoint
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a stipulated recovery state and apply the agreed endpoint for reinstating a baseline directive.

concepts.displayName: Select further imaging from the unresolved biliary question
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a ductal diagnostic question from ongoing gallbladder inflammation and choose noninvasive duct assessment before a therapeutic pathway.

concepts.displayName: Interpret discordant sleep-screen information
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile sleepiness and OSA-probability reports, then document and communicate risk without making a screening diagnosis.

concepts.displayName: Integrate venous and acid-base observations
concepts.learningObjective: Use a reversible position change and a persistent arterial-gas pattern to distinguish two simultaneous laparoscopy physiology mechanisms.

concepts.displayName: Resolve a cystic node before thyroid surgery
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile suspicious nodal morphology with cyst-fluid cytology and select an appropriate ancillary sampling request before planning surgery.

concepts.displayName: Reconcile a benign biopsy with a different palpable lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Match the sampled lesion to the clinical target before choosing further assessment for a concerning imaging-occult finding.

concepts.displayName: Select an offered treatment from the esophageal physiology
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret adequate positional manometry and choose a specific offered treatment for achalasia rather than reflux therapy or palliative pharmacological relaxation.

concepts.displayName: Complete sampling of a changing residual pigmented lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Choose complete diagnostic sampling after a benign limited sector fails to represent a changing residual lesion at a site suitable for excision.

concepts.displayName: Apply leak anatomy to postcholecystectomy treatment
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret duct continuity and adequacy of drainage, then select a procedure for persistent minor leakage.

concepts.displayName: Select the scope of a recurrent venous reflux map
concepts.learningObjective: Use recurrent anatomical distributions and an incomplete prior reflux record to specify the mapping needed before another intervention.

concepts.displayName: Select an archived test for preformed donor reactivity
concepts.learningObjective: Use sample collection time and cellular target to choose a retrospective test of a preimplantation immune mechanism.

concepts.displayName: Recognize an urgent change during cirrhosis optimization
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret new obstructive hernia findings and distinguish emergency assessment from the earlier elective optimization sequence.

concepts.displayName: Interpret a focal collection within a lymphangitic presentation
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a superficial collection from nearby veins on ultrasound and apply the source-control consequence despite a coexisting ascending inflammatory pattern.

concepts.displayName: Use discordant sleep reports in perioperative communication
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish sleepiness from apnoea-probability information and decide what should drive current anaesthetic risk communication without requiring diagnostic confirmation.

concepts.displayName: Separate gas direction from demonstrated acidemia
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a controlled positional filling response and distinguish an acidifying gas change from an acidemic state using laboratory intervals.

concepts.displayName: Resolve thyroid-node specimen discordance
concepts.learningObjective: Use specimen adequacy and an intact-thyroid needle path to interpret discordant node results before selecting lateral-neck surgery or surveillance.

concepts.displayName: Direct inguinal operative anatomy
concepts.learningObjective: Locate a medial groin defect in the posterior inguinal wall using its relationship to the inferior epigastric vessels.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative distension cross-sectional assessment
concepts.learningObjective: Choose broad contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT for stable progressive nonlocalized postoperative symptoms before labeling a fluid complication.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative fluid composition
concepts.learningObjective: Use sampled-fluid triglycerides and directed fluid analysis to distinguish chylous ascites from other postoperative fluid processes.

concepts.displayName: Nutrition for postoperative chylous leakage
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a long-chain-fat-restricted, medium-chain-triglyceride-enriched nutritional strategy within hospital management of a symptomatic postoperative lymphatic leak.

concepts.displayName: Nutrition during prolonged postoperative ileus
concepts.learningObjective: Choose parenteral support when severe prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral nutrition after obstruction and other causes have been assessed.

concepts.displayName: Mesh after a controlled enterotomy
concepts.learningObjective: Choose the supported mesh material when a selected single-stage ventral repair proceeds after securely repaired enterotomy with adequate source control and minimal contamination.

concepts.displayName: Meckel resection extent
concepts.learningObjective: Choose diverticulectomy versus bowel-inclusive resection from disease at the diverticular base and adjacent ileum rather than an isolated width.

concepts.displayName: Celiac serology when IgA is deficient
concepts.learningObjective: Select an IgG-based celiac serologic pathway when IgA deficiency makes a negative IgA result uninterpretable.

concepts.displayName: Celiac testing after gluten withdrawal
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize that negative serology or biopsy after gluten avoidance cannot settle the original celiac question and arrange a supervised diagnostic reassessment.

concepts.displayName: Positive celiac susceptibility typing
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish HLA susceptibility from active celiac disease when deciding whether a positive genotype ends diagnostic evaluation.

concepts.displayName: HCC tumor burden versus liver resection suitability
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish transplant tumor-burden eligibility from a favorable liver-resection profile when portal hypertension and decompensation are present.

concepts.displayName: Structural assessment before gastric emptying
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize when an unresolved mechanical outlet finding prevents attributing retained gastric contents to a motility disorder.

concepts.displayName: Reassessing nutrition after ileus resolves
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess the indication for parenteral nutrition when oral and enteral delivery become adequate after prolonged ileus.

concepts.displayName: Incidental gallbladder muscle invasion
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize muscular invasion as outside the completely resected T1a observation pathway and obtain hepatobiliary surgical review.

concepts.displayName: Gastric cancer with adjacent-organ invasion
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a routine prophylactic organ removal from specialist assessment of direct adjacent-organ invasion during gastric cancer resection planning.

concepts.displayName: Mammographic mass morphology
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate a mass's shape and margin rather than density when deciding which mammographic finding needs diagnostic tissue assessment.

concepts.displayName: Calcification morphology and distribution
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret calcification morphology together with distribution to identify a concerning breast imaging target.

concepts.displayName: Palpable breast mass in the thirties
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a supported diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis and targeted-ultrasound pathway for a new palpable mass in an adult aged 30–39.

concepts.displayName: Benign phyllodes excision planning
concepts.learningObjective: Apply complete excision without a mandated fixed-width margin to a benign phyllodes operative plan.

concepts.displayName: Benign phyllodes margin after excision
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish an isolated positive benign-phyllodes margin from evidence that residual tumor remains when discussing repeat surgery.

concepts.displayName: Borderline phyllodes close-margin action
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the verified close-margin counseling categories after borderline phyllodes excision.

concepts.displayName: Malignant phyllodes close-margin action
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the verified malignant-phyllodes close-margin recommendation while preserving breast-conserving options.

concepts.displayName: Axillary surgery in phyllodes
concepts.learningObjective: Avoid routine sentinel-node or axillary staging for phyllodes when the axilla is nonsuspicious.

concepts.displayName: A suspicious node in phyllodes
concepts.learningObjective: Obtain image-guided needle tissue from a suspicious axillary node despite phyllodes' uncommon nodal spread.

concepts.displayName: Borderline phyllodes operative margin target
concepts.learningObjective: Use the recorded 5-mm borderline-phyllodes counseling target when selecting among feasible breast-conserving excision plans.

concepts.displayName: Malignant phyllodes operative margin target
concepts.learningObjective: Use the recorded 10-mm malignant-phyllodes counseling target when planning complete excision.

concepts.displayName: Phyllodes dissemination pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a distant-organ pattern after malignant phyllodes without assuming axillary negativity excludes metastatic disease.

concepts.displayName: Overt renin-independent aldosterone production
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the recorded overt-phenotype exception to additional aldosterone suppression testing before surgical localization.

concepts.displayName: Factor assessment after an inhibitory mixing pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Choose factor-specific investigation rather than procedural clearance or a final diagnosis from a time-dependent mixing result.

concepts.displayName: New swelling despite established lymphedema
concepts.learningObjective: Investigate an acute postoperative change in a chronically swollen limb before attributing it to established lymphedema.

concepts.displayName: Symptom control versus thyroid-hormone production
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish beta-blocker symptom improvement from disease-directed reduction of thyroid-hormone production when reviewing a Graves regimen.

concepts.displayName: IVC filter versus anticoagulation for a provoked DVT
concepts.learningObjective: Avoid routine IVC-filter placement for a first uncomplicated postoperative proximal DVT when therapeutic anticoagulation is possible.

concepts.displayName: Investigating oxygen-carrying capacity
concepts.learningObjective: Choose direct hemoglobin assessment when a normal pulse-oximeter result is being used to dismiss possible anemia.

concepts.displayName: Tissue sampling after inadequate neck FNA
concepts.learningObjective: Choose selected core needle sampling when repeated FNA does not supply the tissue and ancillary material required to classify an adult neck mass.

concepts.displayName: Perioperative respiratory acid-base trajectory
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a qualitative CO2, pH and bicarbonate trajectory as a respiratory acid-base process rather than inventing a new fixed-acid cause.

concepts.displayName: Reassessing a changing hand burn
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize evolving burn depth from serial raw findings and obtain burn-center consultation for a now-deep hand injury.

concepts.displayName: Paired treatments for urgent VKA reversal
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize intravenous vitamin K as the paired adjunct to rapid factor replacement for emergency VKA reversal.

concepts.displayName: Rapid VKA factor replacement
concepts.learningObjective: Select four-factor PCC for rapid factor replacement in the recorded major-bleeding VKA emergency scope.

concepts.displayName: Early nutrition after an extensive burn
concepts.learningObjective: Choose early enteral nutrition after adequate burn resuscitation when the gastrointestinal tract is usable.

concepts.displayName: Planned thoracic injury exposure
concepts.learningObjective: Choose right thoracic exposure for the recorded stable planned repair of proximal or middle intrathoracic esophageal injury and distinguish resuscitative access.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative SGLT2 restart after a fasting course
concepts.learningObjective: Use present clinical stability and oral intake to determine postoperative SGLT2 resumption rather than carry forward a preoperative interval as an automatic restart clock.

concepts.displayName: Respiratory recurrence after naloxone
concepts.learningObjective: Choose continued monitored respiratory care after an opioid-reversal response rather than infer durable recovery from the first improvement.

concepts.displayName: Ventilation despite a reassuring saturation display
concepts.learningObjective: Select assessment of ventilation when sedation-associated respiratory depression is obscured by a reassuring oxygen-saturation display.

concepts.displayName: Motor reversal versus full anesthetic recovery
concepts.learningObjective: Keep hypnotic and opioid recovery assessment separate after documented reversal of rocuronium blockade.

concepts.displayName: Interpreting matched ventilator pressure changes
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish increased elastic pressure requirements from isolated airway resistance using controlled peak and plateau pressure comparisons.

concepts.displayName: Phosphate chronology before nutrition restart
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish pre-existing phosphate depletion from evidence of a feeding-associated change without dismissing the need for a monitored restart.

concepts.displayName: Perfusion before an early burn-feeding pathway
concepts.learningObjective: Withhold automatic application of the early-enteral burn pathway while shock and resuscitation remain unresolved.

concepts.displayName: Nutrition delivery versus recovery of intestinal function
concepts.learningObjective: Do not infer restored gastrointestinal function from nutritional improvement during parenteral support.

concepts.displayName: Protein adequacy without calorie overfeeding
concepts.learningObjective: Meet the hospitalized conventional-dialysis protein target while preserving an independently assessed energy goal.

concepts.displayName: A collagen cofactor is not universal postoperative therapy
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish an established nutrient requirement from evidence that every adequately nourished postoperative patient needs high-dose supplementation.

concepts.displayName: A new DVT changes anticoagulation purpose
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish prophylactic anticoagulation from treatment of a newly confirmed postoperative proximal DVT.

concepts.displayName: Heparin bridging and VTE prophylaxis are separate
concepts.learningObjective: Keep the decision against routine therapeutic AF bridging separate from indicated postoperative surgical VTE prophylaxis.

concepts.displayName: Factor assays need not wait for a mixing-screen gate
concepts.learningObjective: Arrange appropriate factor-specific assessment without using a mixing study as a mandatory serial gate when factor assays can proceed in parallel.

concepts.displayName: Purulence changes the purpose of wound care
concepts.learningObjective: Respond to a new localized purulent superficial incisional infection with source control rather than extend prophylactic antibiotics as its substitute.

concepts.displayName: Comparing GCS observations with changed testability
concepts.learningObjective: Do not infer neurological deterioration from serial GCS totals when a new airway interference makes the verbal component untestable.

concepts.displayName: A DNR order and treatment before arrest
concepts.learningObjective: Keep an agreed limitation on arrest resuscitation separate from desired treatment of an active surgical problem.

concepts.displayName: A pancreatic cyst that predates pancreatitis
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess the premise of inflammatory-collection drainage when prior imaging shows the pancreatic cyst existed before the pancreatitis episode.

concepts.displayName: A changed course during marginal-ulcer treatment
concepts.learningObjective: Escalate beyond an uncomplicated marginal-ulcer medication pathway when progressive obstructive findings appear despite treatment.

concepts.displayName: Acid suppression after ulcer hemostasis
concepts.learningObjective: Retain indicated PPI treatment after successful high-risk ulcer hemostasis rather than equate immediate bleeding control with completion of ulcer-directed therapy.

concepts.displayName: Duct continuity before a minor-leak stent pathway
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize when demonstrated bile-duct discontinuity prevents applying the preserved-continuity minor-leak ERCP pathway without HPB reassessment.

concepts.displayName: A mucosal specimen does not classify an unsampled wall mass
concepts.learningObjective: Assess whether the submitted gastric specimen represents the wall lesion before using it to clear or initiate targeted tumor treatment.

concepts.displayName: Duct clearance does not remove the gallbladder source
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess the remaining gallbladder treatment indication after common-duct clearance in mild biliary pancreatitis.

concepts.displayName: Antibody results after a valid eradication test
concepts.learningObjective: Do not use antibody serology to overturn an appropriately performed active-infection test of cure and trigger unnecessary repeat eradication.

concepts.displayName: A clear polypectomy site and regional oncologic risk
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish clearance of the local invasive-polyp site from the regional oncologic question created by adverse invasive histology.

concepts.displayName: Continence history before irreversible sphincter division
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess a proposed lateral internal sphincterotomy when baseline leakage and sphincter-injury history put the patient outside the represented low-continence-risk scenario.

concepts.displayName: Matching esophageal provocation to unexplained food symptoms
concepts.learningObjective: Select symptom-matched solid-meal manometry provocation when an adequate ordinary water-swallow series does not explain food-associated obstruction symptoms.

concepts.displayName: Coverage when the recipient bed cannot support a graft
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a reconstructive approach that transfers perfused tissue when the recipient bed cannot support avascular skin transfer.

concepts.displayName: Perfusion after a completely detached tissue transfer
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the vascular reconnection needed by a completely detached vessel-bearing flap rather than apply graft or pedicled-flap assumptions.

concepts.displayName: Operative contamination and a later wound infection
concepts.learningObjective: Keep contamination class at the operation separate from a subsequent surgical-site infection when reconciling wound documentation.

concepts.displayName: A local contrast event despite an allergy label
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a localized injection-site contrast event from a generalized allergic-like event using the actual distribution and timing.

concepts.displayName: T-cell suppression does not establish antibody-pathway control
concepts.learningObjective: Do not use tacrolimus's T-cell target to exclude a separately supported preformed-antibody vascular mechanism in graft injury.

concepts.displayName: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan
concepts.learningObjective: Change an elective incisional-hernia optimization plan when acute irreducibility and obstructive/peritoneal findings develop.

concepts.displayName: Irreversible limb findings and the proposed intervention
concepts.learningObjective: Use a complete irreversible acute-ischemia examination to reject attempted revascularization and obtain vascular assessment of a non-salvage pathway.

concepts.displayName: Reassurance after a negative test
concepts.learningObjective: Calculate negative predictive value using everyone with a negative test rather than all reference-negative or all reference-positive participants.

concepts.displayName: Comparing positive-result frequency across reference groups

decisionNodes.stem: What should be addressed before planning this patient's elective repair?

answerChoices.label: Optimize pulmonary status, then reassess elective repair planning
Schedule repair immediately because the hernia is reducible
Transfer for emergency repair solely because COPD is present
Permanently rule out repair because COPD is an absolute contraindication

decisionNodes.explanation: Pulmonary fitness is a modifiable risk domain in elective incisional-hernia planning. This stable, reducible presentation supports COPD optimization before revisiting repair. Acute irreducibility, obstruction, escalating pain, peritoneal findings, or systemic deterioration requires a different pathway.

resultGateAfter.resultNarrative: Targeted ultrasound shows a round, circumscribed, anechoic cyst with posterior enhancement and no internal solid component, concordant with a simple cyst. The patient says the lump is not painful or bothersome.

decisionNodes.stem: What should you recommend now?

answerChoices.label: Reassure; no cyst-directed procedure is needed
Aspirate the cyst despite the absence of symptoms
Perform core-needle biopsy of the concordant simple cyst
Refer for surgical excision of the simple cyst

decisionNodes.explanation: An imaging-concordant simple cyst that is not painful or bothersome does not need cyst aspiration, core biopsy, or surgical excision. Return the patient to ordinary age- and risk-appropriate care without a cyst-directed procedure.

decisionNodes.stem: How should you counsel this patient about the documented tumor burden?

answerChoices.label: The tumor burden is within standard Milan criteria; refer for transplant-center evaluation
The tumor burden is outside standard Milan criteria because any lesion larger than 3 cm is excluded
The tumor burden is outside standard Milan criteria because solitary HCC is not included
The tumor burden guarantees transplant listing without broader evaluation

decisionNodes.explanation: Standard Milan tumor-burden criteria include one HCC lesion measuring 1 through 5 cm, or two to three lesions each measuring 1 through 3 cm, without macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic disease. Meeting these criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but is not automatic listing. A presentation outside standard Milan criteria still requires specialist assessment rather than an assumption of permanent exclusion.

decisionNodes.stem: How should you interpret this patient's results and proceed?

answerChoices.label: Suspect FHH and arrange genetic testing
Diagnose primary hyperparathyroidism and schedule surgery
Diagnose FHH from the clearance ratio alone

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial correction plan best fits {patientName}'s pre-procedure coagulation record?

answerChoices.label: IV phytonadione followed by repeat coagulation testing
answerChoices.rationale: Obstruction with the selective factor pattern supports a vitamin K-related component. A parenteral route avoids relying on impaired enteral absorption, and the absence of major bleeding or an immediate procedure allows replacement and reassessment rather than automatic plasma. Preserved factor V is supportive, not proof that hepatic synthetic dysfunction is absent. Give IV phytonadione under the applicable monitored protocol; dose, rate, response interval and procedural INR requirement are not scored here.

answerChoices.label: Oral phytonadione followed by repeat coagulation testing
answerChoices.rationale: This addresses vitamin K but relies on absorption through an obstructed-bile context. A parenteral route is the better of the offered replacement plans for this record.

answerChoices.label: Plasma infusion followed by repeat coagulation testing
answerChoices.rationale: Plasma can replace factors promptly, but the current stable nonurgent phase supports trying the likely correctable vitamin K component and measuring the response first. The observation is not a universal prohibition on plasma in jaundice.

decisionNodes.explanation: Standard Milan tumor-burden criteria include one HCC lesion measuring 1 through 5 cm, or two to three lesions each measuring 1 through 3 cm, without macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic disease. Meeting these criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but is not automatic listing. A presentation outside standard Milan criteria still requires specialist assessment rather than an assumption of permanent exclusion.

decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation of the outside specimen should accompany {patientName}'s imaging assessment?

answerChoices.label: Compatible with imaging; lesional histology remains unconfirmed
answerChoices.rationale: The constituents correspond to the overlying mucosa, not a tissue diagnosis of the deeper imaged mass. A locally normal surface specimen does not contradict the integrated classic imaging phenotype.

answerChoices.label: Compatible with imaging; lesional histology is confirmed

answerChoices.label: Inconsistent with imaging; lesional histology remains unconfirmed

answerChoices.label: Inconsistent with imaging; lesional histology is confirmed

decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation of the outside specimen should accompany {patientName}'s imaging assessment?

answerChoices.label: Compatible with imaging; lesional histology remains unconfirmed
answerChoices.rationale: The specimen's actual constituents, rather than its technique label, establish the represented compartment. Normal surface tissue is compatible with the deeper imaged lesion but does not provide its histologic confirmation.

answerChoices.label: Compatible with imaging; lesional histology is confirmed
answerChoices.rationale: This credits the benign or bite-on-bite label as proof that the imaged mass was sampled, without using the listed tissue constituents.

answerChoices.label: Inconsistent with imaging; lesional histology remains unconfirmed

decisionNodes.explanation: The technique name does not establish the depth reached in this particular submitted specimen. The constituents represent surface mucosa. This is neither a universal criticism of bite-on-bite biopsy nor a reason by itself to repeat sampling.

answerChoices.label: Gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication and histologic review
answerChoices.rationale: The fusion is not present in all MALT lymphoma. Negative FISH does not overturn compatible integrated morphology or remove the need for response assessment.

answerChoices.label: Reactive gastritis: infection care and clinical review
answerChoices.rationale: A negative subtype-associated molecular test is not a sensitive exclusion test for MALT lymphoma.

answerChoices.label: Indeterminate infiltrate: repeat fusion testing before treatment
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating the same negative molecular result does not resolve or override the already available integrated tissue findings.

decisionNodes.explanation: Molecular tests have different roles from integrated diagnosis. Use the morphology and clinical extent to plan eradication-led care and histologic response review.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After completed eradication, the urea breath test is negative six weeks after treatment started and two weeks after stopping proton-pump inhibitors. Serial endoscopy shows the gastric ulcer enlarging rather than healing, and recurrent bleeding has lowered hemoglobin. Repeat mapped biopsies show increasing low-grade MALT infiltration. Restaging still confines the disease to the stomach; there is no confluent large-cell component.

answerChoices.label: Involved-site radiotherapy with histologic review
answerChoices.rationale: Localized symptomatic, overtly progressive disease after infection clearance warrants escalation rather than monitoring a regressing residual pattern.

answerChoices.label: Continued surveillance with histologic review
answerChoices.rationale: Observation of asymptomatic residual disease does not apply unchanged to worsening ulceration, bleeding and increasing infiltration.

answerChoices.label: Further eradication therapy with histologic review
answerChoices.rationale: The infection assessment is interpretable; disease progression is not evidence that the same infection treatment needs repetition.

decisionNodes.explanation: Slow histologic clearance and overt progression are different clinical states. Localized gastric MALT with symptomatic or adverse progression after eradication should be assessed for involved-site radiotherapy. Do not infer persistent infection from residual lymphoma or apply watchful monitoring without considering the actual trajectory.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The gastric sections contain a dense small B-cell infiltrate expanding the lamina propria and entering gland epithelium. Larger cells with open chromatin and nucleoli occur singly between the small cells rather than in confluent groups. CD20 marks the infiltrate. H. pylori is detected, and staging shows disease confined to the stomach.
decisionNodes.stem: Which pathology-and-initial-care interpretation should be used for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication and histologic review
answerChoices.rationale: Scattered larger cells do not by themselves establish large-B-cell transformation; integrate the small-cell/gland architecture and localized infection-associated presentation.

answerChoices.label: Gastric large-B-cell lymphoma: systemic lymphoma care
answerChoices.rationale: The mere presence of individual larger cells is not the confluent large-cell component required to establish transformation.

answerChoices.label: Reactive gastric follicles: infection care and clinical review
answerChoices.rationale: The atypical small B-cell expansion with gland invasion is not explained by a reactive-follicle label alone.

decisionNodes.explanation: Gastric lymphoma classification is architectural, not a tally of positive lineage markers or any large cell. A confluent large-B-cell component changes the pathway; individual larger cells among an otherwise small-cell MALT pattern do not establish that change. Localized infection-associated indolent disease is treated with eradication and planned histologic response assessment.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After treatment for localized H. pylori-positive gastric MALT lymphoma, a urea breath test is negative six weeks after therapy started and two weeks after proton-pump inhibitors stopped. The gastric ulcer has healed, the discomfort has resolved and repeat mapped biopsies show smaller residual lymphoid clusters with increasing fibrosis. There is no new deep wall extension or nodal disease on reassessment. The original BIRC3-MALT1 study was negative. PCR still detects the original B-cell clone.
decisionNodes.stem: Which care plan should be arranged for {patientName}'s returned assessment?

answerChoices.label: Active surveillance with repeat gastric biopsies
answerChoices.rationale: The patient is asymptomatic with regressing residual disease and no adverse progression; persistent clonality alone is not an instruction for immediate additional treatment.

answerChoices.label: Involved-site radiotherapy with repeat gastric biopsies
answerChoices.rationale: This treats molecular persistence as sufficient progression despite regressing morphology and resolved symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Further eradication therapy with repeat gastric biopsies
answerChoices.rationale: Infection clearance was assessed under stated conditions; residual lymphoma is not equivalent to persistent infection.

decisionNodes.explanation: The direction of the clinical and histologic response matters. Asymptomatic residual gastric MALT without adverse progression can be monitored after eradication. A persistent molecular clone does not by itself establish a need for radiotherapy, and residual lymphoma does not prove that the infection persists. Planned histologic follow-up remains necessary.

answerChoices.label: Repeat solid-meal scintigraphy under controlled preparation

answerChoices.rationale: A pyloric measurement does not establish that the confounded emptying abnormality persists after reversible factors change.

tissue. This does not promise freedom from later medication. Thyroidectomy and

clinical circumstances and preferences; beta-blocking medication controls
symptoms without lowering thyroid-hormone production.

decisionNodes.stem: What is the appropriate role of RAI in this patient's counseling?

answerChoices.label: RAI is required whenever hyperthyroidism recurs
RAI is excluded after prior antithyroid-drug treatment
RAI is reserved for recurrence after thyroid surgery
RAI can be weighed with antithyroid drugs and surgery

decisionNodes.explanation:
RAI is a reasonable option to discuss after confirmed recurrent
Graves hyperthyroidism following antithyroid-drug withdrawal. It is not
compulsory after every recurrence, excluded because of prior drug treatment, or
reserved until after surgery. The choice among RAI, antithyroid-drug treatment,
and surgery depends on clinical circumstances and the patient's preferences.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should the team choose for {patientName} before the proposed ureteroscopy?

answerChoices.label: Low-dose noncontrast CT reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Current localization can settle whether a procedural target remains after the discordant follow-up evidence.

answerChoices.label: Ureteroscopy as scheduled
answerChoices.rationale: The prior report does not establish the current target in this changed episode or interval course.

answerChoices.label: Cancel ureteroscopy; prevention-clinic follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied reassuring findings do not demonstrate current clearance or resolve the new episode.

This is not a universal requirement for every stone follow-up.

decisionNodes.stem: Which additional MRI comparison should be obtained for {patientName}'s biopsy planning?

answerChoices.label: Axial T1 before and after contrast, both with fat suppression
answerChoices.rationale: A comparison with consistent sequence settings can distinguish intrinsic precontrast brightness from contrast-related change. The outside pair changes both contrast status and suppression, so brightness differences cannot simply be assigned to enhancement.

answerChoices.label: Axial and coronal T1 after contrast, both with fat suppression
answerChoices.rationale: Orthogonal anatomy is useful, but two postcontrast views do not supply a comparable precontrast baseline for the intrinsically bright area.

answerChoices.label: Axial T1 without fat suppression and fluid-sensitive images before contrast
answerChoices.rationale: These contribute tissue characterization but retain an unsuppressed T1 baseline. Different sequence weighting does not supply the comparable pre/postcontrast information needed for this targeting question.

decisionNodes.explanation: Signal differences must be interpreted against how the images were acquired. A bright native T1 region and a postcontrast image with a different suppression setting cannot simply be compared as if contrast were their only difference. Comparable before/after acquisitions can clarify enhancement for the later planning report.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial tissue-sampling plan should the sarcoma team select for {patientName}’s thigh mass?

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
answerChoices.rationale: Both targets enhance. An anterior core biopsy follows the proposed resection exposure: its skin entry and intramuscular tract lie within the proposed specimen. It also avoids crossing the separate medial compartment.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy with a medial approach through adductor longus
answerChoices.rationale: The shorter medial route reaches more intensely enhancing tissue, but crosses adductor longus outside the proposed specimen. That tract would not be removed with the currently planned specimen.

answerChoices.label: Open incisional biopsy with an anterior approach through rectus femoris
answerChoices.rationale: The anterior skin entry and intramuscular tract are inside the proposed specimen, but an initial image-guided core is preferred when percutaneous sampling is feasible. Open incisional biopsy is a selected alternative, not the initial choice on these findings.

answerChoices.label: Open incisional biopsy with a medial approach through adductor longus
answerChoices.rationale: This combines an open initial procedure despite feasible core access with a medial tract through adductor longus outside the proposed specimen.

decisionNodes.explanation: Choose image-guided core sampling through the anterior approach. Both targets enhance; the stronger enhancement and shorter medial route do not outweigh tract planning. The biopsy tract, including its skin entry, must be removable with the definitive specimen. The stated anterior resection includes that tract; staying in the tumor-bearing compartment by itself would not establish this. Feasible core sampling is the preferred initial method; selected cases may require open biopsy.

decisionNodes.stem: Which type of hernia do the ultrasound findings identify in {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should be offered for {patientName}'s groin hernia at this visit?

answerChoices.label: Plan elective hernia repair
answerChoices.rationale: The established femoral anatomy supports timely elective repair despite improved function. The reducing, nontender presentation without obstructive features does not establish an emergency.

answerChoices.label: Plan scheduled hernia surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: Observation can be appropriate for selected minimally symptomatic inguinal hernias in men. Improvement in lifting does not extend that observation rule to the identified femoral route.

answerChoices.label: Plan emergency hernia exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The femoral type warrants repair planning, but the current record does not show the persistent painful irreducible or obstructed presentation needed to favor emergency exploration here.

decisionNodes.explanation: Combine the established type with the current acuity. A stable reducing femoral hernia warrants timely elective repair planning even when symptoms have improved. decisionNodes.stem: Which repair should be discussed for {patientName}’s recurrent groin defect?

answerChoices.label: Totally extraperitoneal repair
answerChoices.rationale: The old report describes an anterior mesh plane. A posterior preperitoneal approach is the offered route that avoids re-entering that operated plane for a symptomatic recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Lichtenstein mesh repair
answerChoices.rationale: This is a valid primary repair, but repeating the anterior mesh approach re-enters the prior operative plane in this recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Shouldice tissue repair

decisionNodes.explanation: The current functional episode remains consistent with the demonstrated hernia rather than being dismissed because hip disease also exists. This does not establish TEP as superior to every other posterior approach or promise that hernia repair cures the separate hip ache.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The catheter tip remains above the diaphragm throughout the outside recording. Blind advancement stopped after repeated retching. During swallows, pressure rises simultaneously in the recorded esophageal channels.
decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should guide procedural planning for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopically assisted manometry
answerChoices.rationale: Junction-crossing manometry can provide the relaxation and body measurements absent from this recording. Assisted placement addresses the documented technical failure.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagram with a barium tablet
answerChoices.rationale: Emptying and tablet passage can corroborate obstruction, but the prior contrast study already shows retention and this does not provide the missing manometric phenotype.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Regurgitation can tempt reflux testing, but it does not resolve junction relaxation and contractile classification after this technically failed pressure study.

decisionNodes.explanation: The observed pressure events cannot classify junction relaxation when the catheter has not crossed it. Assisted catheter placement can permit the manometric assessment needed for procedural planning. Contrast emptying and reflux monitoring answer other questions. This comparison makes no claim that manometry universally precedes FLIP after every failed attempt.

answerChoices.label: Single wet swallows after baseline recovery
answerChoices.rationale: Separated swallows assess ordinary swallow-induced peristalsis; overlapping swallows can inhibit a developing contraction.

answerChoices.label: Multiple rapid swallows followed by a recovery swallow

decisionNodes.explanation: The acquisition sequence changes how absence of contraction is interpreted. decisionNodes.stem: Which primary-site procedure should be arranged next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Excisional biopsy of the complete lesion
answerChoices.rationale: The sampled sector is epidermis confined, but its report does not establish the invasive status of the raised residual component. Complete diagnostic removal is feasible and can supply the architecture and maximum invasion information needed before selecting treatment extent.

answerChoices.label: Wide local excision for melanoma in situ
answerChoices.rationale: This converts a valid local epidermal diagnosis into a whole-lesion treatment classification before the raised residual focus is represented. A therapeutic plan based on that extension may use the wrong disease extent.

answerChoices.label: Full-thickness incisional biopsy of the raised focus
answerChoices.rationale: Targeting the raised component is a credible way to seek invasion information, but it again samples part of a lesion whose complete diagnostic removal is feasible, leaving whole-lesion architecture and maximum depth less fully represented.

decisionNodes.explanation: The represented dermis is explicitly free of the atypical melanoma cells, so the local epidermal diagnosis is supported. That does not classify a separate residual focus. answerChoices.label: Melanocytic atypia shown; residual-lesion invasion unassessed

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Two mapped outside specimens are available. The earlier full-thickness punch from one sector contains invasive melanoma measuring 1.8 mm from the granular layer to the deepest tumor; that fragment's deep edge is free of tumor. A later shave from another sector measures 0.6 mm to melanoma at its deep cut surface. A firm focus remains in the residual lesion. No regional node is palpable at this visit. Completion sampling is being arranged.
decisionNodes.stem: Which provisional depth and nodal-discussion entry should accompany {patientName}'s completion-sampling request?

answerChoices.label: At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported
answerChoices.rationale: The greatest demonstrated invasive extent is not erased by a later shallower transected fragment. Even though the whole-lesion maximum is not final, the established depth is already in the range supporting a sentinel-node discussion in this clinically node-negative setting.

answerChoices.label: At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported
answerChoices.rationale: The general discussion direction does not repair the depth record: this drops the greater demonstrated invasive extent simply because another specimen was later or transected.

answerChoices.label: At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
answerChoices.rationale: This preserves the demonstrated extent but treats uncertainty about a possibly greater maximum as a reason to ignore a discussion boundary already crossed by known evidence.

answerChoices.label: At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
answerChoices.rationale: This both replaces the greater demonstrated extent with a later smaller value and uses incomplete maximum-depth assessment to defer an already supported discussion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Integrate the mapped specimens rather than replace one with the latest report. The 1.8-mm invasive measurement remains demonstrated; a 0.6-mm tumor-positive cut base cannot lower it. The whole-lesion maximum may still increase. The existing greater-than-1-mm guidance supports discussing sentinel-node staging in this clinically node-negative setting while primary assessment continues. It does not order a nodal procedure or determine how a later abnormal node should be assessed.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management should be recommended now for {patientName}'s calcium disorder?

answerChoices.label: Biochemical surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: The biochemical/longitudinal pattern and pathogenic CASR result support confirmed uncomplicated familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia. Observation with follow-up calcium measurements is appropriate for that state. Age under 50 supports parathyroidectomy in confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, not in every cause of high calcium. The localization focus does not establish a coexisting operative disease, and the normal DXA is not the reason to avoid surgery.

answerChoices.label: Elective parathyroidectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Young age and a focal localization study make this a credible plan if the disorder is assumed to be primary hyperparathyroidism. Those findings do not override the recorded inherited disorder. Parathyroid surgery usually does not correct uncomplicated FHH; a new progressive pattern or a separately established coexisting disorder would require reassessment.

answerChoices.label: Cinacalcet therapy
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent hypercalcemia can tempt a medication choice when surgery is not selected. The described stable, asymptomatic inherited disorder is usually observed with calcium follow-up rather than treated simply to normalize the laboratory number.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s pancreatic cyst findings now?

answerChoices.label: Continue MRI-based cyst surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: Routine surveillance is insufficient for the combined high-risk findings in a surgical candidate.

answerChoices.label: Arrange EUS-guided cyst-fluid sampling
answerChoices.rationale: Sampling can help unresolved risk classification, but the MRI already supplies two independently high-risk findings. Negative fluid would not erase them.

decisionNodes.stem: Which pancreatic-remnant management plan should be recommended for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Completion pancreatectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Low-grade margin dysplasia and an unconcerning remnant cyst do not establish a need to remove the remaining pancreas.

answerChoices.label: MRI-based surveillance of the pancreatic remnant
answerChoices.rationale: Resected IPMN still warrants remnant surveillance; the low-grade margin and low-risk remnant do not by themselves select completion surgery.

answerChoices.label: Discharge from pancreatic imaging follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The absence of invasive cancer does not remove the remnant risk associated with IPMN.

decisionNodes.explanation: Low-grade IPMN at a margin is not equivalent to invasive cancer at a margin. With no concerning remnant finding, surveillance preserves the opportunity to detect later disease without automatic completion pancreatectomy. Postresection IPMN follow-up differs from a completely resected noninvasive MCN.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan best addresses {patientName}'s pancreatic lesion and current symptoms?

answerChoices.label: Continue pancreatic MRI surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: The phenotype is reassuring for malignancy, but surveillance does not address demonstrated symptomatic compression.

answerChoices.label: Arrange endoscopic cystgastrostomy
answerChoices.rationale: A microcystic epithelial lesion is not an inflammatory collection that can be treated by cystgastrostomy.

answerChoices.label: Refer for pancreatic cyst resection
answerChoices.rationale: A convincingly serous lesion can still require surgery when it causes adjacent-organ compression and symptoms.

decisionNodes.explanation: The microcystic, central-scar pattern favors a serous lesion. Usually benign behavior does not eliminate the mechanical indication: the lesion narrows the stomach and symptoms match that site. Resection evaluation is appropriate; a benign epithelial cyst is not managed as a pseudocyst.
