decisionNodes.stem: Which paired interpretation best fits {patientName}'s record?

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac filling; increased respiratory elastic load
answerChoices.rationale: Smaller filling volume with preserved ejection fraction supports reduced preload rather than a new loss of contractility. The increased plateau pressure at the same delivered volume supports an elastic-load component.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac contractility; increased respiratory elastic load
answerChoices.rationale: The respiratory interpretation fits. Smaller end-diastolic volume with similar ejection fraction does not best support primary loss of contractility as the explanation of lower stroke volume.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac filling; increased respiratory resistive load
answerChoices.rationale: The filling interpretation fits. A new resistive load does not by itself account for the higher plateau pressure under the supplied ventilation controls.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac contractility; increased respiratory resistive load
answerChoices.rationale: Both are real contributors to perioperative deterioration, but neither is the best primary account of the supplied paired observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: The fall in stroke volume accompanies a smaller end-diastolic volume with a similar ejection fraction, supporting reduced filling rather than new primary contractile failure. Higher plateau pressure at unchanged tidal volume and PEEP indicates an increased elastic pressure requirement. The reversible pressure sequence fits abdominal venous-return restriction and respiratory mechanical restriction, without proving a unique vascular lesion or excluding every mixed mechanism.

decisionNodes.stem: Which endoscopic intervention should be planned for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Biliary plastic stenting
answerChoices.rationale: The anatomy supports internal diversion of a communicating minor leak. A stent can be inserted without dividing the papilla, avoiding the additional sphincterotomy bleeding exposure while anticoagulation remains necessary.

answerChoices.label: Biliary sphincterotomy
answerChoices.rationale: Papillary division can lower resistance but creates a higher-bleeding-risk intervention here. It is not interchangeable with stent diversion in this anticoagulated patient.

answerChoices.label: Covered biliary metal stenting
answerChoices.rationale: Covered metal stents have a role in selected complex or refractory leaks. Ongoing output after external drainage does not by itself establish failure of initial plastic-stent diversion.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: In the outside record, Simon Hale is at the end of the second full day after drainage of a postoperative abdominal collection. The completion study showed no residual locule or continuing bowel communication. He is afebrile, eating and improving without another infectious focus. Meropenem was started at source control; the specimen was obtained on first cavity entry before its first dose. The constructed report below is complete for the recovered organisms. The team is selecting the antibacterial regimen for the remainder of the post-control course.

answerChoices.label: Ceftriaxone plus metronidazole
answerChoices.rationale: Both recovered organisms are covered, and the source and clinical course support dropping unnecessary antipseudomonal/carbapenem coverage while a post-control course remains in progress.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: During the outside admission, a purulent subcutaneous incisional pocket was opened and decompressed, and piperacillin-tazobactam was administered. Across the examinations before that procedure and at the recorded reassessment, {patientName}'s fever and deep left pelvic pain persisted while incisional pain and redness diminished. Blood pressure was maintained without vasopressors, and tenderness remained confined to the lower abdomen without generalized guarding. The CT report obtained at that reassessment is shown below. Antibacterial therapy and incisional wound care continued under all plans.
decisionNodes.stem: At that recorded reassessment, which management plan was most appropriate for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Image-guided pelvic drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Improvement at the opened incision does not establish drainage of the pelvic compartment. The persisting deep symptoms and the fluid, debris and inflammatory findings in a different compartment support an unaddressed focal infection. Its confined distribution, the examination and the reported access anatomy favor image-guided drainage while antibacterial care continues. Failure to demonstrate contrast escape does not exclude an occult communication; deterioration or diffuse contamination would require renewed operative assessment.

answerChoices.label: Antibacterial treatment with reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The observed local improvement concerns the decompressed incisional pocket. The deeper collection and continuing pelvic symptoms are not accounted for by that procedure, so another medical-only reassessment leaves this source unaddressed.

answerChoices.label: Operative abdominal exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The anterior route crosses bowel, but the same report describes a posterior soft-tissue corridor. With confined disease and the documented examination, that alternative access supports a directed procedure rather than abdominal exploration.

decisionNodes.explanation: Improvement at the opened incision does not establish drainage of the pelvic compartment. decisionNodes.stem: Which additional toxicology-directed medication is reasonable for {patientName}'s recurrent rhythm while electrical treatment, lipid therapy and resuscitation continue?

answerChoices.label: Intravenous sodium bicarbonate
answerChoices.rationale: AHA describes bicarbonate as a reasonable adjunct for life-threatening wide-complex tachycardia from local-anesthetic toxicity. This addresses the exposure/conduction problem during, not instead of, electrical and supportive treatment.

answerChoices.label: Intravenous lidocaine
answerChoices.rationale: Lidocaine is familiar from other ventricular-arrhythmia care, but adding another local anesthetic is avoided during local-anesthetic systemic toxicity.

answerChoices.label: Intravenous magnesium sulfate
answerChoices.rationale: The described uniform rhythm does not show the polymorphic twisting pattern associated with torsades; magnesium does not address the demonstrated local-anesthetic sodium-channel toxicity as directly.

answerChoices.rationale: Confuses the source of newly absorbed nutrients with the redistribution explaining the serum fall.

decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation of {patientName}'s renal phosphate handling is supported by these results?

answerChoices.label: Renal phosphate loss is inappropriately high.
answerChoices.rationale: Fractional phosphate excretion is (10 x 1.0)/(1.0 x 20) x 100 = 50%. With concurrent serum phosphate of 1.0 mg/dL, that is inappropriate loss rather than the expected conservation. It does not identify the cause of the renal loss or exclude concurrent redistribution.

answerChoices.label: Renal phosphate conservation is appropriately increased.
answerChoices.rationale: This anchors on nutrition restart and its familiar cellular-shift explanation without testing the renal response. Creatinine-normalized phosphate excretion is 50%, not the low excretion expected during this degree of hypophosphatemia.

answerChoices.label: Renal phosphate handling remains unclassifiable here.
answerChoices.rationale: This assumes a timed urine collection is required before any interpretation. Simultaneous phosphate and creatinine concentrations permit fractional-excretion assessment; the supplied pretreatment samples show inappropriate loss. They do not quantify daily phosphate balance.

decisionNodes.explanation:
Fractional phosphate excretion = (urine phosphate x serum creatinine)/(serum phosphate x urine creatinine) x 100 = (10 x 1)/(1 x 20) x 100 = 50%.
At a low simultaneous serum phosphate, the kidney should conserve phosphate; this result supports a renal-loss component.
Feeding-associated cellular uptake can coexist, but does not account for this renal response. The samples assess current handling, not daily phosphate balance or the specific cause of loss.

decisionNodes.stem: Which safety method fits reconstruction of {patientName}'s completed emergency-referral close call and its contributing systems problems?

answerChoices.label: Root cause analysis
answerChoices.rationale: The review starts with a specific completed close call and reconstructs how referral-priority and handoff systems contributed. That is the retrospective purpose of RCA.

answerChoices.label: Healthcare failure mode and effects analysis
answerChoices.rationale: Healthcare FMEA anticipates possible process failures prospectively. This review instead starts with a particular close call that already occurred.

answerChoices.label: Individual performance audit
answerChoices.rationale: The described review examines contributing referral-priority and handoff systems. An individual performance judgment alone does not describe that event-centered systems purpose.

answerChoices.label: Patient satisfaction survey
answerChoices.rationale: The patient asks about reconstruction of a specific safety event. Measuring satisfaction would answer a different question from how the systems contributed.

decisionNodes.explanation: This is root cause analysis: reconstruction of a completed close call to identify systems contributors. The review is retrospective, rather than a prospective assessment of possible future failures.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Root cause analysis starts with an event or close call that already happened and reconstructs contributing systems problems. Here the referral handoff is the starting event. Remember: start with what happened and examine how the process contributed. Healthcare FMEA instead looks ahead for possible process failures; neither label is a verdict of individual blame.

decisionNodes.stem: Which safety method fits advance assessment of possible failures in {patientName}'s planned immunosuppression handoff process?

answerChoices.label: Healthcare FMEA
answerChoices.rationale: The team is anticipating ways a process might fail before using it. That prospective process-centered task fits healthcare FMEA.

answerChoices.label: Root cause analysis
answerChoices.rationale: RCA reconstructs a completed event or close call. No such event is the starting point of this planned workflow assessment.

answerChoices.label: Individual performance audit
answerChoices.rationale: The planned task examines potential failures across process steps. It is not primarily an assessment of one worker's performance.

decisionNodes.stem: What is root cause analysis intended to assess in {patientName}'s completed delayed-message event?

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct the event and its systems contributors
answerChoices.rationale: RCA works backward from the completed routing event to examine how systems contributed. It is broader than assigning an individual performance verdict.

answerChoices.label: Predict failures before launching an untested process
answerChoices.rationale: That anticipatory task describes healthcare FMEA. This document instead starts with a particular routing event that has already occurred.

answerChoices.label: Compare satisfaction scores across completed clinic visits
answerChoices.rationale: Comparing satisfaction does not reconstruct the delayed-message event or identify its contributing systems problems. It answers a different review question.

answerChoices.label: Judge an individual worker's performance in isolation
answerChoices.rationale: Individual blame is not RCA's central purpose. Restricting the review to one worker leaves its contributing systems question unanswered.

decisionNodes.explanation: RCA reconstructs the completed delayed-message event and examines systems contributors. It does not primarily forecast a new workflow or decide blame for one worker in isolation.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: An RCA label identifies a retrospective systems question: what happened in this event, and which process problems contributed? The delayed message event is its starting point. Remember to look beyond a worker in isolation. The method's purpose does not, by itself, establish legal liability, assign individual blame, or guarantee that improvement has occurred.

decisionNodes.stem: Why can this patient's normal SpO2 coexist with reduced oxygen-carrying content?

answerChoices.label: Fewer hemoglobin carriers can have normal saturation
Normal saturation establishes a normal hemoglobin quantity
Reduced hemoglobin requires reduced oxygen saturation
The saturation percentage directly measures hemoglobin quantity

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Fewer hemoglobin carriers can have normal saturation.” Saturation describes how fully the available hemoglobin is occupied. Anemia reduces the available carrier quantity, so a normal fraction does not establish normal oxygen content.

decisionNodes.stem: Which reversal instruction should guide {patientName}'s care while assisted ventilation continues?

answerChoices.label: Withhold flumazenil
answerChoices.rationale: Midazolam was used to control a potentially life-threatening seizure state; antagonizing it is contraindicated even though respiratory support is needed.

answerChoices.label: Administer flumazenil now
answerChoices.rationale: Respiratory depression does not remove the contraindication when the benzodiazepine was required for seizure control.

answerChoices.label: Administer flumazenil after another antiseizure drug

decisionNodes.explanation: The reason a benzodiazepine was administered changes whether its antagonist is appropriate. Repeated convulsions without recovery of awareness required seizure control; flumazenil is contraindicated when benzodiazepines are used to control a potentially life-threatening condition such as status epilepticus. Maintain supported ventilation and specialist seizure/anesthesia care. Boosted exposure increases the temptation to reverse sedation, but does not override this boundary.

decisionNodes.stem: Which revision best addresses {patientName}'s two proposed midazolam routes under her current medication regimen?

answerChoices.label: Omit oral midazolam; start with smaller IV increments
answerChoices.rationale: Oral midazolam is contraindicated with darunavir/cobicistat. For repeated parenteral midazolam, close monitoring and dose-reduction consideration are required; smaller initial increments followed by response titration are a concrete lower-exposure plan rather than copying pre-interaction dosing.

answerChoices.label: Retain oral midazolam; start with smaller IV increments
answerChoices.rationale: Reducing parenteral exposure does not remove the oral-midazolam contraindication under the current regimen.

answerChoices.label: Omit oral midazolam; start with the copied IV increments
answerChoices.rationale: This correctly removes oral midazolam but carries pre-cobicistat repeated IV dosing into the new interaction context. The label calls for dose-reduction consideration, especially with repeated administration; the lower starting-increment plan addresses that risk explicitly.

answerChoices.label: Retain oral midazolam; start with the copied IV increments
answerChoices.rationale: The oral route remains contraindicated, and the copied pre-interaction repeated IV plan fails to address increased or prolonged sedation risk. Monitoring does not erase the route-specific contraindication.

decisionNodes.explanation: The cobicistat-containing regimen changes both comparisons. Omit oral midazolam; it is contraindicated. Monitored IV midazolam remains an option, with dose reduction considered especially for repeated use. Smaller initial increments followed by observation and titration address the new exposure risk. This is an individualized plan, not a universal dose or a reason to interrupt antiretroviral therapy.

decisionNodes.stem: Which correction best addresses the claim that sugammadex binds every neuromuscular blocker?

answerChoices.label: Its binding is selective for rocuronium and vecuronium
Its binding applies equally to cisatracurium and succinylcholine
Its binding applies equally to atracurium and mivacurium

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Its binding is selective for rocuronium and vecuronium.” The selectivity should not be extrapolated to cisatracurium. decisionNodes.stem: Why can hypnotic sedation persist after sugammadex reverses rocuronium blockade?

answerChoices.label: Sugammadex antagonizes propofol at its receptor

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Blocker binding leaves propofol sedation.” Neuromuscular reversal and emergence from hypnosis are different processes. Blocker complex formation does not establish accelerated hypnotic clearance. The represented binding targets are neuromuscular blockers, not propofol. Blocker binding is not direct reversal of hypnotic receptor effects.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnosis is best supported by this skin biopsy?

answerChoices.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates skin location, morphology and the panel; no single stain alone establishes the diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Metastatic pulmonary small-cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant melanoma
answerChoices.rationale: A malignant skin nodule remains plausible initially, but the combined epithelial/neuroendocrine staining favors another lineage.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant lymphoma
answerChoices.rationale: Small dermal malignant cells can suggest a lymphoid process before the integrated immunophenotype is considered.

decisionNodes.explanation: The morphology and combined CK20, synaptophysin and TTF1 pattern favor Merkel cell carcinoma among these options. Staining patterns have exceptions; no single marker definitively excludes pulmonary small-cell carcinoma or establishes Merkel cell carcinoma. Integrate the panel with the clinical and pathologic assessment.

answerChoices.rationale: Treats a normal examination as sufficient regional assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which mechanical effect explains a greater pressure requirement for the same tidal volume during evaluated pneumoperitoneum?

answerChoices.label: Cephalad diaphragm shift with lower compliance
Caudal diaphragm shift with greater compliance
Increased lung volume with unchanged chest mechanics
Increased chest compliance with easier lung expansion

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Cephalad diaphragm shift with lower compliance.” Abdominal insufflation can restrict respiratory expansion. That is the opposite of the described restrictive effect. The pressure-volume change reflects altered mechanics. Greater compliance would not explain the increased pressure requirement.

decisionNodes.stem: Which effect of abdominal insufflation is consistent with the documented reduction in respiratory compliance?

answerChoices.label: Downward diaphragm displacement freeing lung expansion
Expansion of resting lung volume without pressure effects
Removal of chest-wall restriction by increased abdominal pressure

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Upward diaphragm displacement restricting lungs.” Mechanical compression changes respiratory expansion. This would not match the restrictive physiology. The summary specifically describes reduced compliance. Increasing abdominal pressure can impose restriction instead.

decisionNodes.stem: Which effect explains the pressure-volume change rather than the added CO2 load itself?

answerChoices.label: Reduced compliance from cephalad diaphragm movement
Increased compliance from a caudally displaced diaphragm
Improved compliance from greater diaphragm excursion
Expansion of lung volume without altered respiratory mechanics

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Reduced compliance from cephalad diaphragm movement.” Gas absorption and restrictive mechanics are distinct consequences of insufflation. The documented pressure requirement points toward restriction. The documented mechanical effect reduces rather than improves expansion and compliance. The pressure-volume relation changed in this course.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnosis best explains Ella Morgan's abdominal-wall lump?

answerChoices.label: Epigastric hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Uses the focal upper-midline fat-containing wall defect; the previous incision is at a different site.

answerChoices.label: Spigelian hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a lateral abdominal-wall defect near the semilunar line with the observed midline defect.

answerChoices.label: Incisional hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Overweights the operative history without matching the current defect to the prior incision.

answerChoices.label: Lumbar hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a posterior or flank wall defect with the anterior upper-midline finding.

decisionNodes.explanation: The focal upper-midline fat-containing defect supports epigastric hernia. decisionNodes.stem: Which biochemical study should be prioritized next in {patientName}'s preoperative assessment?

answerChoices.label: Baseline serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone
answerChoices.rationale: The 46,XX result with nonpalpable gonads changes the explanation of the external anatomy. Screen for an adrenal steroid disorder rather than assuming the unseen gonads are testes.

answerChoices.label: Baseline serum anti-Mullerian hormone
answerChoices.rationale: AMH can assess testicular tissue in a different nonpalpable-gonad context; it does not take priority over the adrenal screen raised by this completed 46,XX result.

answerChoices.label: Cosyntropin-stimulated adrenal steroid profile
answerChoices.rationale: A stimulated full profile helps when the initial screen is borderline or further characterization is needed; the supported initial screen has not been obtained in this stable child past infancy.

decisionNodes.explanation: The chromosome result prevents assuming that bilateral nonpalpable gonads are simply undescended testes. An adrenal cause of virilization needs evaluation. For a stable symptomatic child past infancy, the Endocrine Society supports baseline early-morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone by LC-MS/MS as the initial screen; borderline results need further specialist testing. This is one prioritized step within full multidisciplinary assessment, not a complete DSD workup or a decision about gender identity or genital surgery.

decisionNodes.stem: Which revascularization priority best fits {patientName}'s event and completed evaluation?

answerChoices.label: Right endarterectomy with early scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: The cover-eye history localizes the transient deficit to the right eye. The recent symptomatic right lesion has priority despite the larger asymptomatic measurement on the left.

answerChoices.label: Left endarterectomy with early scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the larger numerical stenosis as the symptomatic target despite the event localization.

answerChoices.label: Right endarterectomy with deferred scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: The current lack of recurrent symptoms does not erase the significance of the recent symptomatic severe lesion.

answerChoices.label: Left endarterectomy with deferred scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: This both assigns the wrong side to the event and defers the symptomatic-lesion assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: Covering the unaffected eye left the impaired right eye in use; covering the right eye restored vision through the left. The right carotid lesion is therefore the recent symptomatic severe lesion. Prompt endarterectomy assessment together with medical therapy is appropriate for this represented operative context; the opposite side's larger percentage does not establish symptom causation. The four side/timing combinations are balanced rather than allowing majority-component assembly.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should precede a decision to operate on {patientName}'s nodule?

answerChoices.label: Tc-99m heat-damaged red-cell scintigraphy
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent hemolysis after total splenectomy and the blood-film clue raise the possibility of functioning residual splenic tissue. The selected functional study can address tissue identity before a nodule-directed procedure.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic-ultrasound-guided core biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: This moves to invasive tissue sampling before the selected noninvasive splenic-function study for the represented postoperative hematologic pattern.

answerChoices.label: Pancreatic-protocol magnetic resonance imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Further morphology may characterize a pancreatic lesion, but the immediate clinical question is whether functioning splenic tissue accounts for this constrained post-splenectomy pattern.

decisionNodes.explanation: The laboratory course indicates recurrent hemolysis in a patient whose original hereditary spherocytosis remains supported. Absent Howell-Jolly bodies is a clue, not proof of a causal remnant. Heat-damaged red-cell scintigraphy is the selected study for functioning residual splenic tissue before a nodule-directed operation. A positive study would still need correlation with the symptomatic hemolysis before any removal decision.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next test pathway should {patientName} be offered?

answerChoices.label: Arrange germline testing after genetic counseling
answerChoices.rationale: The internally controlled protein-loss pattern is a hereditary signal, not a germline result. Constitutional evaluation addresses that signal rather than repeating a tumor screen or assigning the daughter's status.

answerChoices.label: Arrange microsatellite-instability testing on the tumor block
answerChoices.rationale: This supplies another tumor-screen measure rather than answering the unresolved constitutional question after the interpretable suggestive result.

answerChoices.label: Arrange four-protein immunohistochemistry on another tumor block
answerChoices.rationale: The paired controls support interpreting the current result; repeating tumor staining does not establish inherited status.

decisionNodes.explanation: The controls stain, while the tumor loses MSH2 and MSH6. That interpretable pattern warrants genetics counseling and germline assessment; it is not itself an inherited variant or a family-testing result. Another tumor-screen assay does not answer the constitutional question. The item does not choose a specific panel or claim that every such tumor has a germline cause.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should {patientName} undergo before the next treatment is selected?

answerChoices.label: Repeat esophagogastroduodenoscopy with multiple tissue biopsies
answerChoices.rationale: The new material does not securely classify the changed lesion. More diagnostic tissue is needed before treating it as the same low-grade process or selecting a staging pathway for a different one.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound for wall depth and regional-node staging
answerChoices.rationale: This could contribute to staging a classified local lymphoma, but depth information does not resolve the changed lesion's uncertain histology.

answerChoices.rationale: Systemic distribution may become important, but it does not replace an adequate classification of the scant crushed lesion sample.

decisionNodes.explanation: The outside label exceeds what the small crushed sample establishes. New large atypical cells in a changed lesion require adequate tissue classification before the next lymphoma plan. Repeat endoscopy with biopsies is supported when gastric MALT classification is uncertain. Neither local-depth imaging nor metabolic staging replaces that step. No specific transformation diagnosis, radiation regimen or systemic drug treatment is asserted.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic blood-testing plan should {patientName}'s team arrange?

answerChoices.label: tTG-IgG/deamidated gliadin peptide IgG assay panel with gluten reintroduction
answerChoices.rationale: This corrects both the antibody-class limitation and the changed exposure that can suppress disease-test findings. A specialist directs the exposure plan; no challenge dose or interval is specified.

answerChoices.label: tTG-IgG/deamidated gliadin peptide IgG assay panel with continued gluten avoidance
answerChoices.rationale: The antibody class is changed appropriately, but the shared dietary limitation in disease testing remains.

answerChoices.label: tTG-IgA/endomysial IgA assay panel with gluten reintroduction
answerChoices.rationale: The exposure is addressed, but both assays still depend on an immunoglobulin class below detection.

answerChoices.label: tTG-IgA/endomysial IgA assay panel with continued gluten avoidance
answerChoices.rationale: This preserves both limitations in the negative result: deficient IgA and restricted testing exposure.

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret two independent preanalytic conditions before replacing the test. Switching to IgG does not repair gluten withdrawal, and restoring exposure does not repair absent IgA. The named IgG panel with specialist-directed reintroduction addresses both. Further adult confirmation follows the results; no universal challenge dose or duration is invented.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic plan should the hospital use next for {patientName}'s vomiting?

answerChoices.label: Repeat endoscopy with pyloric biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The first procedure ended because of retained contents, not an impassable proven stricture. Decompression changes the acquisition conditions, and the irregular structural lesion warrants direct assessment and tissue.

answerChoices.label: Contrast fluoroscopy with pyloric transit mapping
answerChoices.rationale: Fluoroscopy can characterize transit, but contrast already passes and it would not characterize the irregular mural lesion histologically.

answerChoices.label: Prepared four-hour gastric-emptying scintigraphy
answerChoices.rationale: This is the appropriate physiology protocol after structural exclusion; diabetes and retained food do not supply that prerequisite.

decisionNodes.explanation: Retained food in diabetes does not establish gastroparesis. The first examination was preparation-limited; decompression and persistent contrast passage support a prepared repeat examination rather than treating prior termination as proof that endoscopic access is impossible. Assess and sample the irregular pyloric lesion before moving to emptying physiology. This is a diagnostic plan, not an instruction to force a scope through a tight obstruction.

decisionNodes.stem: Which group most warrants repeat representative sampling before {patientName}'s treatment plan is finalized?

answerChoices.label: Repeat vacuum sampling of group A
answerChoices.rationale: Specimen calcium confirms calcium acquisition, but arterial-wall calcium does not explain the target's nonvascular branching ductal pattern. This is a concordance problem after apparent technical success.

answerChoices.label: Repeat vacuum sampling of group B
answerChoices.rationale: The rim appearance and oil-cavity wall histology provide a coherent benign explanation. Benign wording is not itself a reason to resample.

answerChoices.label: Repeat vacuum sampling of group C
answerChoices.rationale: The tissue explains the suspicious calcification target. Its malignancy requires treatment planning but does not make repeat diagnostic acquisition the priority over the unexplained target.

decisionNodes.explanation: Calcium in a specimen and an appropriately placed clip do not by themselves establish radiology-pathology concordance. Compare what produced the calcification histologically with its imaged morphology. Group A remains unexplained, whereas B and C have findings that account for their patterns. Renew representative sampling of A before basing the treatment extent on a benign label.

answerChoices.rationale: Initial correction after PCC does not establish sustained restoration of vitamin-K-dependent production. Unreliable oral delivery and rebound without redosing support IV vitamin K rather than automatic repeat factor loading.

answerChoices.label: Repeat four-factor PCC with serial INR testing
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the later INR as proof that more rapid factor loading is required despite achieved hemostasis and an unresolved sustained-reversal component.

answerChoices.label: Plasma factor replacement with serial INR testing
answerChoices.rationale: Plasma can supply factors in emergency reversal, but it does not directly correct the unreliable vitamin-K component and adds volume without the current rapid-replacement indication.

decisionNodes.explanation: Do not infer durable reversal from an early INR after factor replacement. The observed emesis does not prove zero absorption, but it makes the oral dose unreliable; the later INR rise without warfarin redosing is consistent with an inadequately secured sustained-reversal component. In the represented controlled-bleeding stage, give IV phytonadione and follow the INR rather than reflexively repeat factor loading. New major bleeding or another urgent intervention would change the immediate replacement question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which empagliflozin schedule should be agreed for {patientName}'s next procedure?

answerChoices.label: Continue interruption until ERCP with oral-recovery restart
answerChoices.rationale: The next fasting procedure is too near to restart safely now; restarting afterward depends on recovered intake and clinical state.

answerChoices.label: Resume until ERCP morning with oral-recovery restart
answerChoices.rationale: The eventual recovery condition is appropriate, but resuming until the procedure morning fails the recorded advance interruption requirement.

answerChoices.label: Continue interruption until ERCP with glucose-triggered restart
answerChoices.rationale: The preprocedure interruption fits, but a glucose rise does not establish recovery of intake and clinical state.

answerChoices.label: Resume until ERCP morning with glucose-triggered restart
answerChoices.rationale: This combines inadequate advance interruption with a restart criterion that does not establish postoperative recovery.

decisionNodes.explanation: Reconcile both procedures rather than treating the first recovery as the end of the medication problem. Empagliflozin labeling advises interruption for at least three days when possible before surgery or a procedure associated with prolonged fasting. A new dose 48 hours before the next fasting procedure would interrupt that protection. After the second procedure, resumption again depends on clinical stability and oral intake, not glucose in isolation.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use the support and perfusion trajectory together. A soft abdomen at A does not override worsening circulatory observations. decisionNodes.stem: Which reconciliation of the heparin orders fits {patientName}'s recorded indications?

answerChoices.label: Stop therapeutic heparin; continue prophylactic enoxaparin
answerChoices.rationale: Routine full-intensity bridging is not established by this history, whereas the cancer operation supplies a different preventive indication.

answerChoices.label: Continue therapeutic heparin; cancel prophylactic enoxaparin
answerChoices.rationale: A treatment-level anticoagulant would subsume prophylaxis while given, but this assigns therapeutic bridging to an interruption without the represented indication.

answerChoices.label: Defer both heparin prescriptions during initial warfarin resumption
answerChoices.rationale: Correctly avoiding routine bridging does not remove the separately represented postoperative prophylaxis indication.

decisionNodes.explanation: Read the order's purpose rather than the subtherapeutic INR as a universal heparin trigger. Routine bridging for the represented atrial-fibrillation interruption is not supported. Postoperative cancer-surgery prophylaxis has a separate purpose while the INR remains subtherapeutic. Cancel the therapeutic bridge order and retain the prophylactic prescription with routine prescribing review. The case does not direct overlapping heparin regimens or prescribe a dose, start interval or duration.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next investigation should guide {patientName}'s persistent postoperative drainage?

answerChoices.label: Arrange hepatobiliary-contrast magnetic resonance cholangiography
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent bile plus a duct segment outside the filled endoscopic tree requires an anatomical study that can map upstream segments and localize excreted biliary contrast, rather than assume the filled main duct represents every source.

answerChoices.label: Arrange repeat endoscopic retrograde cholangiography contrast study
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating injection from the same downstream lumen can again fail to show a source outside the communicating filled tree.

answerChoices.label: Arrange hepatobiliary scintigraphy for leakage
answerChoices.rationale: This can demonstrate activity of a leak but provides less spatial information for the branch relationship needed before another intervention.

decisionNodes.explanation: Do not equate a main-duct injection without visible escape with absence of every biliary source. The drainage and the nonrepresented segment create an anatomical question that the same downstream injection may not answer. Hepatobiliary-contrast MRCP can localize leakage and evaluate duct relationships before the team selects a minor-leak stent or a different HPB pathway. The schematic does not itself prove a particular repair or mandate an operation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which data-preparation plan is needed before the team compares infection rates in {patientName}'s operative wound-class stratum?

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from intraoperative findings
answerChoices.rationale: Later infection selectively changes the new-period predictor; reconstructing the same operation-time variable restores comparable classification without relabeling the outcome.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct both periods from later readmission reports
answerChoices.rationale: Applying outcome-driven recoding to both periods makes the coding rule consistent but still moves infected cases out of their original risk strata.

answerChoices.label: Retain final classes and adjust for the number of readmissions
answerChoices.rationale: A count adjustment does not undo selective movement of infections between operative strata.

decisionNodes.explanation: Classify contamination at the operation and preserve the later infection as an outcome. Gross operative spillage is not converted retrospectively into a pre-existing dirty/infected operation because a wound later becomes infected. In the new-period dataset, selectively moving infected cases changes the denominator and outcomes within the apparent original class. Reconstruct comparable operation-time classifications before comparing rates; this does not by itself prove the prevention program caused any benefit. The audit-bias application is an explicit local synthesis, not a published performance estimate.

cases.displayName: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan

The operative team had not yet closed the abdomen.

answerChoices.label: Temporary abdominal closure with planned re-exploration

decisionNodes.explanation: Urgent transfer has already occurred; the decision is now whether to commit to definitive closure. Read the reversible pressure response at fixed ventilation together with bowel that still requires reassessment during resuscitation. Those findings support a temporary closure and planned re-exploration pathway, rather than applying a selected one-stage hernia repair rule to this different physiology. This new closure-stage teaching point requires targeted verification and surgical sign-off. No pressure threshold, re-exploration interval, mesh prohibition for every emergency repair or clinic-based operative capability is asserted.

decisionNodes.stem: Which negative predictive value and protocol action apply to {patientName}'s negative screen?

answerChoices.label: 90.3% NPV; obtain contrast CT under the study protocol
answerChoices.rationale: For symptom workup, 112 of 124 negative screens are reference-negative: NPV 90.3%, residual frequency 9.7%, above the stated protocol trigger.

answerChoices.label: 98.7% NPV; repeat CRP surveillance under the study protocol
answerChoices.rationale: This imports the routine-screening group's 152/154 NPV and misses the higher residual frequency in the group corresponding to this order.

answerChoices.label: 80.0% NPV; obtain contrast CT under the study protocol
answerChoices.rationale: 48/60 is sensitivity in the symptom-workup group. It conditions on reference-positive cases rather than on this patient's negative result.

decisionNodes.explanation: First match the order's purpose to the study population, then condition on a negative result. The symptom-workup row has 112 true-negative and 12 false-negative screens: 112/(112+12) is 90.3%, leaving 9.7% reference-positive among negative screens. That exceeds this fictional protocol's 5% trigger, so its next step is contrast CT. The 98.7% result belongs to a different population, and 80% is sensitivity, not NPV. These constructed frequencies are not an individual's validated leak probability or a safe clinical discharge rule.

decisionNodes.stem: Which post-test probability and protocol action follow from {patientName}'s positive screen?

answerChoices.label: 56%; CT acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: Sensitivity is 40/80 and false-positive rate 20/200, so LR+ is 5. Prior odds 1/4 become 5/4; probability is 5/9, approximately 56%.

answerChoices.label: 33%; repeat CRP assay
answerChoices.rationale: Using the raw positive counts 40/20 as the likelihood ratio gives 2 and then post-test odds 1/2, but the unequal reference-group sizes require rates.

answerChoices.label: 67%; CT acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: 40/60 is the positive predictive value within the validation sample. Its selected reference-group mix differs from the patient's stated prior odds.

decisionNodes.explanation: Calculate conditional rates before updating this patient's prior odds. Sensitivity is 0.5 and the false-positive rate is 0.1, giving LR+ 5. Multiplying pretest odds 1:4 by 5 gives 5:4; 5/(5+4) is approximately 56%. That reaches this fictional protocol's CT branch. Dividing raw positive counts happens to work only under special sample-size relationships and fails here. The validation sample's 40/60 positive fraction also uses a different prior mix. The result depends on the stated transport assumption and supplies no real test validation or patient-risk estimate.

cases.displayName: A paired binary change needs a paired analysis
cases.presentation: {patientName}, a 62-year-old man, reviews a clinic medication-reconciliation pilot in which his record participated. A pharmacist established a reference medication list for each of 100 patients using interview and medicine-container review. For each reference record, the same clerk first entered a preoperative medication list by the old workflow, then re-entered it using the proposed checklist; an independent pharmacist compared both versions with the same reference. The binary endpoint was omission of at least one current prescribed medicine versus no such omission. Record identifiers were retained. A fictional feasibility plan advances to a controlled study only if the proportion without an omission improves by at least 10 percentage points; otherwise the checklist is revised. This is not a causal trial or permission for clinical rollout.

decisionNodes.stem: Which analysis and next-phase decision fit the paired medication-list audit discussed with {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: McNemar analysis with checklist revision
answerChoices.rationale: The repeated binary outcome is paired; 12 improve and five worsen, so net improvement is seven percentage points, below the fictional 10-point requirement.

answerChoices.label: Fisher exact analysis with checklist revision
answerChoices.rationale: The net-change branch fits but treating marginal before/after outputs as independent loses each record's linkage.

answerChoices.label: McNemar analysis with controlled-study advancement
answerChoices.rationale: This respects pairing but counts 12 improvements without subtracting the five new omissions.

answerChoices.label: Fisher exact analysis with controlled-study advancement
answerChoices.rationale: This combines loss of pairing with counting improvements without offsetting deterioration.

decisionNodes.explanation: The two medication-list outputs refer to the same patient reference record, so they are not independent samples. McNemar's paired-binary analysis uses the discordant outcomes. The no-omission proportion rises from 48/100 to 55/100: a seven-point net improvement after accounting for five records that worsened. The fictional plan therefore calls for checklist revision before a controlled phase. Repeating the task in the same order may introduce learning and order effects; this uncontrolled audit does not establish causal benefit, regardless of the selected paired analysis.

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret each endpoint against its own prespecified criterion. The recovery 90% interval is entirely within -2 to +2 days, meeting the stated TOST equivalence condition. decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should be selected next for {patientName}'s swallowing symptoms?

answerChoices.rationale: EGD is often the initial investigation for persistent esophageal dysphagia, but the observed delayed return makes initial contrast assessment of a suspected proximal pouch the better offered sequence. FEES and EGD are distinct examinations.

answerChoices.rationale: The body is separable while neck/duct anatomy remains unresolved; subtotal surgery is an accepted offered bailout that avoids hazardous division there.

answerChoices.rationale: A change in dissection direction does not by itself solve the unresolved final neck/duct junction that a total operation must address.

answerChoices.label: Neck-first total cholecystectomy
answerChoices.rationale: The apparent funnel is not reliable identification when the broad duct is being tented into it and its junction remains unresolved.

decisionNodes.explanation: A funnel-shaped appearance does not resolve the junction when traction tents a broad duct and the neck plane remains fused. Avoid division of unidentified structures. decisionNodes.stem: Which mesh should be used for {patientName}’s selected single-stage repair?

answerChoices.label: Macroporous monofilament polypropylene mesh
answerChoices.rationale: The controlled event falls within the selected single-stage scope, and the reconstructed posterior layer separates this extraperitoneal prosthesis from bowel. Permanent macroporous synthetic reinforcement is supported in that selected context.

answerChoices.label: Microporous expanded polytetrafluoroethylene mesh
answerChoices.rationale: Selecting a visceral-contact material misreads the extraperitoneal pocket and does not address the contamination-related material comparison.

answerChoices.rationale: The recognized and controlled bowel event does not establish a benefit from substituting biologic mesh for the supported permanent macroporous synthetic option.

decisionNodes.explanation: The repaired opening, controlled spill and unchanged physiology define the selected single-stage scope. The closed posterior layer also places the implant outside the peritoneal cavity. Choose macroporous monofilament polypropylene rather than defaulting to biologic material or selecting a visceral-contact material for a compartment separated from bowel. This does not select repair timing after an uncontrolled enterotomy.

answerChoices.rationale: This is recurrent focal bleeding after initial conventional hemostasis, with poor superficial purchase. Cap-mounted clipping offers a repeat endoscopic approach before declaring repeat therapy unsuccessful.

answerChoices.rationale: The separating superficial edges make repeating the same type of purchase less persuasive in this recurrent setting.

decisionNodes.stem: Which operative plan should be selected from {patientName}’s current cholangiogram?

answerChoices.label: De-air the injection system and repeat ductal imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Changing lucencies near injection suggest an artifact, and duodenal flow does not establish complete proximal coverage. Improve the study before deciding on duct treatment.

answerChoices.label: Proceed to common-bile-duct exploration for the filling defects
answerChoices.rationale: This acts on transient injection-associated lucencies before confirming a genuine ductal lesion on an adequate study.

answerChoices.label: Complete the cholecystectomy after documenting free duodenal flow
answerChoices.rationale: Duodenal passage does not answer the incomplete proximal anatomy or settle the apparent defects.

decisionNodes.explanation: The transient moving lucencies near the injection tip can be air, while flow into the duodenum does not establish that both proximal ductal trees were shown. De-air and obtain a complete repeat study before committing to duct exploration or accepting the image as reassuring. The guideline supplies quality requirements and artifact concerns; the repeat-injection sequence is an original clinical application of those requirements.

decisionNodes.stem: Which bedside assessment should guide the decision about another fluid bolus for {patientName} at this stage?

answerChoices.label: Track pulse-pressure variation from the arterial waveform
answerChoices.rationale: Both the irregular rhythm and spontaneous breaths disturb the cyclic relationship needed to interpret this displayed value. A large number does not establish fluid responsiveness under these conditions.

answerChoices.label: Track stroke-volume change during passive leg raising
answerChoices.rationale: A reversible change in preload can be assessed through direct flow measurement despite the represented breathing pattern and rhythm. The later treatment decision still requires assessment of perfusion need and fluid risk.

answerChoices.label: Track respiratory variation of inferior vena-caval diameter
answerChoices.rationale: Inspiratory effort and other cardiopulmonary factors affect vena-caval variation. It is less dependable for this decision than a direct reversible flow-response test.

decisionNodes.explanation: The waveform value is affected by both irregular beats and spontaneous respiratory effort. Measure the change in stroke volume during passive leg raising. This answers whether flow responds to preload under the actual acquisition conditions.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next resuscitation adjustment best fits {patientName}'s current pressure, flow response and respiratory course?

answerChoices.label: Give a balanced-crystalloid bolus
answerChoices.rationale: The flow response is genuine, but it does not establish that another bolus offers the best risk-benefit balance. Worsening oxygen needs and new diffuse lung findings after fluids argue against further empiric volume loading here.

answerChoices.label: Start a dobutamine infusion
answerChoices.rationale: The represented low pressure occurs with vigorous contraction and substantial measured output. There is no demonstrated low-output cardiac dysfunction to make an inotrope the preferred adjustment.

answerChoices.label: Increase the norepinephrine infusion
answerChoices.rationale: The low MAP needs pressure support while the large flow response is weighed against the deteriorating respiratory course. Norepinephrine titration addresses the current hypotension without another empiric fluid load.

decisionNodes.explanation: The reversible flow rise shows preload responsiveness. The worsening respiratory course after fluid changes whether that response should be pursued with another bolus. Titrate norepinephrine for the current low pressure while reassessing the evolving physiology.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management pathway should be recommended for {patientName} after review of the separately labelled surgical specimens?

answerChoices.label: Multidisciplinary review for follow-up without resection
answerChoices.rationale: Margin-negative noninfiltrative disease confined to an intact appendix could support this pathway. The separate diaphragmatic nodule contains mucinous epithelium, so the appendix margin and negative pelvic nodule cannot establish confinement.

answerChoices.label: Multidisciplinary review for right hemicolectomy and nodes
answerChoices.rationale: The whole appendix does not show destructive glandular invasion requiring the localized adenocarcinoma nodal pathway. The demonstrated tumor is in a separate surface deposit; a regional colectomy does not by itself address that distribution.

answerChoices.label: Multidisciplinary review for cytoreduction and intraperitoneal therapy
answerChoices.rationale: Low-grade mucinous epithelium in the separately labelled diaphragmatic nodule demonstrates cellular disease outside the appendix. This requires experienced-center assessment for cytoreduction with or without intraperitoneal treatment. Histology, extent and operative feasibility determine the final plan; the biopsy does not guarantee eligibility.

decisionNodes.explanation: The specimens represent different sites. A negative pelvic nodule and a clear appendiceal margin do not negate low-grade mucinous epithelium in the diaphragmatic nodule. That finding changes the disease field beyond the appendix. Experienced-center assessment for cytoreduction and possible intraperitoneal therapy is appropriate; this is not a promise of HIPEC or evidence that every deposit has been sampled. Regional colectomy is not a substitute for evaluating the demonstrated surface disease.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Dedicated liver MRI obtained after the staging CT resolves both previously indeterminate lesions. Each has uniform low T1 and high T2 signal, a smooth thin wall, and no mural nodule or enhancement on the acquired precontrast and postcontrast series. The remainder of liver MRI and chest, abdominal and pelvic staging shows no additional lesions. The whole appendix specimen contains a 2.6-cm well-differentiated grade-1 neuroendocrine tumor with a clear base margin; the mesoappendix was removed. {patientName} has recovered and remains fit for surgery.
decisionNodes.stem: Which next management plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s appendiceal tumor after these acquired staging results?

answerChoices.label: Finish resection with appendectomy and follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The liver findings have benign cyst morphology, but the completely measured primary is larger than the guideline boundary for appendix-only treatment. A clear base does not address regional nodal risk.

answerChoices.label: Proceed with right hemicolectomy and regional nodes
answerChoices.rationale: The acquired MRI observations characterize the represented liver lesions as simple cysts rather than leaving them indeterminate for staging. In this fit patient, the whole-specimen tumor size supports regional resection despite a clear appendectomy margin.

answerChoices.label: Obtain liver core biopsy before further resection
answerChoices.rationale: These are resolved fluid-signal, nonenhancing lesions without internal solid tissue on adequate MRI, not persistent indeterminate targets. Biopsy would add an unsupported staging step. This conclusion comes from morphology, not a negative receptor scan.

decisionNodes.explanation: The earlier CT uncertainty must be updated using the actual MRI: simple fluid signal, a thin wall and no enhancing internal tissue characterize the represented lesions as cysts. This is different from inferring cysts from absent receptor uptake. The whole-specimen primary exceeds the directly sourced greater-than-2-cm NET boundary, so regional nodal resection remains indicated despite a clear base margin. A smaller favorable tumor or unresolved liver staging would change this decision.

answerChoices.rationale: The record now shows established worsening post-extubation respiratory failure in the population where rescue NIV may delay needed reintubation.

answerChoices.rationale: Preventive NIV evidence does not justify delaying reintubation for established failure in this non-COPD medical record.

decisionNodes.explanation: This is rescue after deterioration, not prevention immediately after planned extubation. In general non-COPD medical patients with established post-extubation failure, ERS/ATS conditionally discourages NIV that may delay reintubation. The worsening ventilation and fatigue make continued oxygen escalation inadequate in this record. COPD and postoperative exceptions must not be erased.

decisionNodes.stem: Which tube-management plan should {patientName}'s outside-hospital team choose next?

answerChoices.label: Retain the tube; obtain contrast CT mapping
answerChoices.rationale: An unintended organ trajectory requires defining the injury and vascular relationships before controlled tube management. Keep the tube in place while urgent cross-sectional assessment and the relevant surgical teams establish that plan.

answerChoices.label: Remove the tube; obtain ultrasound reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Removing a catheter that traverses an organ before defining the injury can worsen bleeding; a stable examination is not proof that blind removal is safe.

answerChoices.label: Retract the tube; obtain repeat chest radiographs
answerChoices.rationale: Blind partial withdrawal still moves the tube through the unintended organ tract, and radiography does not define the unresolved hepatic vascular relationship.

decisionNodes.explanation: The ultrasound describes an organ-traversing catheter, not a simple inadequate pleural drain. Keep it in place while urgent cross-sectional imaging and the relevant surgical teams define a controlled management plan.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: {patientName} has recovered from the hemorrhagic phase and maintains perfusion without vasopressors. Multimodal analgesia, regional anesthesia and respiratory rehabilitation continue. CT documents several ipsilateral segmental rib fractures with severe displacement. Lung opacities and oxygen requirements have improved. During two supervised liberation trials, a chest-wall segment moves inward with inspiration as breathing becomes shallow and the cough weakens. Both trials are stopped for respiratory distress.
decisionNodes.stem: Which next treatment plan best fits {patientName}'s hospital recovery findings?

answerChoices.label: Rib stabilization followed by ventilator-liberation trials
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent mechanical chest-wall instability during failed liberation despite analgesic treatment supports stabilization assessment during this admission. Improving parenchymal disease strengthens the importance of the persistent chest-wall findings.

answerChoices.label: Current ventilatory support with further liberation trials
answerChoices.rationale: Nonsurgical care is appropriate for many rib injuries. Here, repeated failure despite the ongoing treatment and persistent chest-wall instability support adding fixation assessment.

answerChoices.label: Tracheostomy followed by prolonged ventilator weaning
answerChoices.rationale: Tracheostomy may support prolonged ventilatory needs. It does not address the persistent displaced unstable chest-wall segment demonstrated during these trials.

decisionNodes.explanation: The lung findings have improved while the displaced segment still moves paradoxically during failed liberation attempts despite analgesic care. That pattern supports rib-stabilization assessment as the next addition to care. Analgesia and rehabilitation continue, and tracheostomy remains a separate option for prolonged support requirements.

decisionNodes.stem: Which infusion change should have followed {patientName}'s recorded treatment response?

answerChoices.label: Add intravenous nicardipine infusion
answerChoices.rationale: Rate has entered the guideline target range while pressure remains uncontrolled; added vasodilation addresses the remaining treatment target after beta blockade.

answerChoices.label: Increase the intravenous esmolol infusion
answerChoices.rationale: Escalating rate-slowing therapy does not best address the remaining pressure target once the recorded rate response is adequate and perfusion is preserved.

answerChoices.label: Replace esmolol with intravenous diltiazem
answerChoices.rationale: The record does not demonstrate beta-blocker intolerance or a rate-control failure requiring substitution; it shows persisting pressure elevation after a rate response.

decisionNodes.explanation: Rate and pressure are separate treatment targets. The observed rate response is within the guideline range, while pressure remains elevated. Add an intravenous vasodilator after initial beta blockade rather than simply intensifying rate reduction or substituting another rate-control agent. Nicardipine provides additional blood-pressure reduction while beta blockade continues.

decisionNodes.stem: Which left-subclavian strategy should have accompanied {patientName}'s elective TEVAR plan?

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian bypass before aortic coverage
answerChoices.rationale: LSA interruption threatens inflow to the patent LIMA graft supplying an occluded native LAD territory.

answerChoices.label: Aortic coverage, then bypass if arm ischemia develops
answerChoices.rationale: An arm-symptom trigger does not protect the LIMA-dependent coronary circulation during elective coverage.

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian transposition before aortic coverage
answerChoices.rationale: Transposition requires proximal subclavian clamping, which can interrupt the patent pedicled LIMA coronary inflow; bypass avoids that required interruption.

decisionNodes.explanation: Protect the pedicled LIMA coronary inflow before elective LSA coverage. Bypass avoids the proximal subclavian clamp required for transposition; waiting for arm ischemia also fails to protect this coronary-dependent territory.

decisionNodes.stem: Which immediate rescue plan should have been activated for {patientName}'s postoperative findings?

answerChoices.label: Vasopressor-supported perfusion with CSF-drainage rescue
answerChoices.rationale: The pattern points to spinal-cord perfusion injury; pressure support and reduction of intrathecal pressure address that mechanism.

answerChoices.label: Esmolol-based pressure reduction with intravenous analgesia
answerChoices.rationale: Further pressure reduction would work against perfusion rescue in this new postoperative neurologic syndrome.

answerChoices.label: Heparin anticoagulation with urgent aortoiliac thrombectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Warm feet and preserved pulses make aortoiliac occlusion a poorer explanation than spinal perfusion injury.

decisionNodes.explanation: Bilateral leg weakness after hypotension with preserved limb pulses raises concern for spinal-cord ischemia. Activate perfusion rescue and specialist CSF-drainage assessment; the new phase calls for restoring cord perfusion rather than intensifying impulse reduction.

decisionNodes.stem: Which repair approach should have been preferred for {patientName}'s intact thoracoabdominal aneurysm?

answerChoices.label: Open thoracoabdominal graft replacement
answerChoices.rationale: Heritable native-aorta disease in an operable patient favors open reconstruction when repair is required.

answerChoices.label: Branched endovascular thoracoabdominal repair
answerChoices.rationale: Technical feasibility does not erase the guideline preference for open repair in this heritable native-aorta setting.

answerChoices.label: Visceral debranching with thoracic endografting
answerChoices.rationale: A hybrid operation still relies on endograft sealing in the diseased native aorta rather than providing the preferred open reconstruction.

decisionNodes.explanation: For an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome, the checked multisociety guideline favors open repair. Native-aortic tissue disease and long-term durability matter even when branched or hybrid reconstruction is technically possible.

answerChoices.label: Biopsy segment VI; classify segment II by imaging

answerChoices.label: Biopsy segment II; classify segment VI by imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Sampling the larger classic-pattern lesion leaves the non-HCC-specific segment VI lesion without tissue classification. Size alone does not select the diagnostic target.

answerChoices.label: Biopsy both lesions; defer classification of each

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret each lesion independently. The segment II nonrim-enhancement/washout pattern in cirrhosis supports an imaging diagnosis; the segment VI rim-enhancing pattern indicates malignancy without establishing its histologic type. Obtain tissue from segment VI before choosing tumor-specific treatment. Optional sampling of an imaging-characteristic HCC for another clinical purpose is a separate decision.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial treatment plan best fits {patientName}'s pancreatic-head cancer findings?

answerChoices.label: Upfront resection with venous reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: This potentially reconstructable venous pattern is not a simple clearly resectable relationship. Neoadjuvant therapy and reassessment are generally favored over proceeding directly to a technically complex operation.

answerChoices.label: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with surgical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The venous abnormality with preserved adjacent segments and separated arteries supports a potentially reconstructable borderline pattern. Begin systemic treatment, then reassess staging and technical resectability.

answerChoices.label: Palliative chemotherapy with response assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Venous involvement alone does not establish permanent unresectability. The supplied negative distant staging and potentially reconstructable local pattern retain a possible resection pathway.

decisionNodes.explanation: The venous contour change and short narrowed segment suggest borderline local anatomy rather than either a clear surgery-first relationship or necessarily permanent unresectability. Neoadjuvant systemic treatment with restaging and surgical reassessment is the best offered sequence. Patency above and below supports consideration of reconstruction; it does not guarantee technical feasibility, which requires specialist review.

Before treatment begins, pruritus and jaundice increase. Imaging shows intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile-duct dilation above the distal stricture. decisionNodes.stem: Which pre-treatment management plan is best for {patientName} at this visit?

answerChoices.label: ERCP metal stenting before chemotherapy
answerChoices.rationale: Obstructive jaundice should be relieved before the planned neoadjuvant course. A self-expanding metal stent offers more durable drainage through that treatment interval than a plastic stent.

answerChoices.label: ERCP plastic stenting before chemotherapy
answerChoices.rationale: Plastic stenting can decompress the duct but is more prone to occlusion during a prolonged neoadjuvant interval. The planned course makes durable metal-stent drainage preferable here.

answerChoices.label: Begin chemotherapy with bilirubin reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has progressive obstructive jaundice before a multi-cycle course. Reassessment alone does not first relieve the obstruction or provide durable drainage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Progressive jaundice with upstream dilation represents clinically important biliary obstruction even without cholangitis. Drain it before the planned neoadjuvant course. Endoscopic self-expanding metal stenting is preferred to plastic stenting for durable drainage through that interval. This comparison does not establish one metal-stent design as universally best and does not create a numerical bilirubin rule.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan should have been recommended for {patientName} at this point in the hospital course?

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus image-guided catheter drainage
answerChoices.rationale: The existing catheter drains a different collapsed compartment. Persistent infection with a separate collection needs effective source control; image-guided access is the less invasive initial approach in this stable record.

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus interval imaging reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The record contains ongoing infection with a separate undrained collection. The presence of an existing catheter does not establish source control when its side holes are confined to another compartment.

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus operative washout and drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Operative source control is a real option, but stable physiology without generalized peritonitis and an available image-guided approach favor a minimally invasive attempt first. This is not a requirement to delay surgery if the situation changes.

decisionNodes.explanation: The catheter's side holes are in the collapsed anterior space, while the infected-appearing collection occupies a separate posterior compartment. Antibiotics and the existing catheter have therefore not established adequate source control. Image-guided catheter drainage is the preferred initial addition in this stable hospital record. IR must choose new placement or exchange from the actual anatomy; the question does not promise that repositioning through the old tract will work. Operative drainage remains appropriate if interventional control fails or surgical indications develop.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should next inform care for {patientName}'s persistent dysphagia?

answerChoices.label: High-resolution manometry during a standardized solid meal
answerChoices.rationale: A solid-meal extension can expose meal-related physiology missed by routine liquid swallows. Here the adequate positional study already demonstrates a retained-peristalsis outflow pattern with reproduced symptoms. Independent supportive obstruction evidence, rather than additional pressure provocation, is needed to establish its clinical relevance.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Reflux monitoring can address a reflux hypothesis, but it does not establish whether the current preserved-peristalsis outflow pattern impedes passage.

answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: Elevated outflow pressure with retained peristalsis is not conclusive achalasia. Even with relevant symptoms, the manometric outflow-obstruction pattern needs accepted supportive evidence that passage is impaired. Timed barium with a tablet addresses that question before treatment is chosen.

decisionNodes.explanation: Preserved propagated contractions change the interpretation of the raised outflow pressures. A symptomatic manometric EGJ outflow-obstruction pattern remains clinically inconclusive until supported by an accepted complementary obstruction assessment. Timed barium with tablet passage supplies that assessment. Meal provocation can address unexplained meal symptoms, while reflux monitoring answers a different physiologic question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should next inform care for {patientName}'s continuing dysphagia?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound of the cardia and junction wall
answerChoices.rationale: An infiltrative junction process can mimic a motor disorder despite an unrevealing mucosal examination. EUS is useful when clinical or imaging findings raise that concern. The represented gradual, weight-stable course and prior structural assessment provide no new wall target; the outstanding gap is usable physiology after failed assisted manometry.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic FLIP topography and junction distensibility
answerChoices.rationale: Retention has been documented but usable pressure physiology has not been acquired despite assisted placement. FLIP is a supported complementary assessment of junction opening and motor response in this circumstance. It neither supplies a complete manometric subtype nor by itself authorizes myotomy.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Regurgitation can reflect reflux, but the acquired retained-column pattern and incomplete motor assessment leave obstructive physiology unresolved. Reflux burden and symptom association do not characterize that opening problem.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: In the outside record, Dana Mercer is on post-control day 2 after drainage and closure of a leaking small-bowel source. Fever and pain are improving. The cavity specimen was processed for aerobic culture only; it grew Pseudomonas susceptible to cefepime and ciprofloxacin. The inpatient medication list includes ongoing sotalol for a prior arrhythmia. Renal function permits the offered drugs. The team is choosing an IV regimen for the remaining post-control treatment.
decisionNodes.stem: Which IV antibacterial regimen best fits Dana Mercer's source, available microbiology and current medication list?

answerChoices.label: Cefepime plus metronidazole
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the susceptible aerobic isolate and retains enteric anaerobic coverage without adding the ciprofloxacin-sotalol QT interaction.

answerChoices.label: Ciprofloxacin plus metronidazole
answerChoices.rationale: The combination can cover susceptible complicated intra-abdominal pathogens, but the concurrent sotalol makes ciprofloxacin an avoidable QT-risk choice here.

answerChoices.label: Cefepime
answerChoices.rationale: It avoids the ciprofloxacin interaction and covers the recovered Pseudomonas, but it does not supply the anaerobic component required by this enteric source.

answerChoices.label: Ciprofloxacin
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the susceptible Pseudomonas but omits the enteric anaerobic component and adds the concurrent-sotalol safety problem.

decisionNodes.explanation: The culture-processing history cannot exclude anaerobes from a leaking enteric source; cefepime needs an anaerobic partner here. decisionNodes.currentUpdate: In the outside record, Adrian Cole has undergone operative closure of a postoperative bowel leak and drainage of an abdominal collection. Piperacillin-tazobactam is active against the recovered bacteria. He remains febrile and requires norepinephrine after fluid resuscitation. The specimen obtained by direct needle entry into the previously undrained cavity, before any catheter was placed, grows C. glabrata; antifungal susceptibilities are pending. He recently received fluconazole during this admission. The team is reassessing the current antimicrobial plan while continuing source follow-up.
decisionNodes.stem: Which antimicrobial plan is most appropriate now for Adrian Cole at this recorded stage?

answerChoices.label: Continue piperacillin-tazobactam and add micafungin
answerChoices.rationale: The fresh normally sterile cavity isolate in a patient with persistent severe infection warrants antifungal treatment. An echinocandin is the preferred offered initial choice with pending susceptibility, recent azole exposure and current vasopressor requirement.

answerChoices.label: Continue piperacillin-tazobactam without an antifungal
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the bacteria but dismisses yeast recovered directly from a previously undrained infected cavity while severe illness persists. This is not a longstanding drain-isolate scenario.

answerChoices.label: Continue piperacillin-tazobactam and add fluconazole
answerChoices.rationale: Antifungal treatment is justified, but initial fluconazole is less appropriate with C. glabrata susceptibility still unknown, recent azole exposure and ongoing vasopressor requirement.

decisionNodes.explanation: The decisive source fact is direct first access to a previously undrained infected cavity, rather than a device culture. Together with persistent severe illness, that supports treatment of intra-abdominal Candida. Among these plans, micafungin supplies the preferred initial class for this C. glabrata/azole-exposure/pending-susceptibility context. Fluconazole is conditional on a different susceptibility and clinical setting; piperacillin-tazobactam has no antifungal role.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Maya Grant completed four full days of active antibacterial treatment after drainage of her postoperative collection and has been off treatment since then. At clinic she is afebrile, eating and has less pain; her leukocyte count remains above the laboratory reference range but continues to fall. The completion study documented an emptied cavity without an ongoing leak. The retained catheter was left for output/removal follow-up. A specimen later collected from its disinfected sampling port, after the catheter had remained in place throughout recovery, reports Pseudomonas susceptible to cefepime and meropenem. No new collection was accessed and no blood cultures were obtained. Clinical and drain follow-up continue with every plan.
decisionNodes.stem: Which antibacterial plan is most appropriate for Maya Grant now?

answerChoices.label: Do not restart antibacterial therapy
answerChoices.rationale: A current port isolate from an indwelling system does not establish a new source infection. Her improving course after adequate control and completed treatment does not justify restarting solely for the report or a declining mildly abnormal inflammatory marker.

answerChoices.label: Restart IV cefepime
answerChoices.rationale: Cefepime is active against the isolate, but the report's device provenance and current recovery do not establish an indication to treat it.

answerChoices.label: Restart IV meropenem
answerChoices.rationale: Meropenem is active, but greater spectrum does not overcome the missing evidence of recurrent infection and would treat an indwelling-system result.

decisionNodes.explanation: Collection technique and source validity are separate. Disinfecting the port does not make material from a longstanding catheter equivalent to direct access to a new cavity. Interpret that report with Maya's clinical recovery, documented control and completed course: do not restart for susceptibility results or a falling leukocyte count in isolation. New illness would require reassessment rather than automatic dismissal of future cultures.
